text: I'm not sure what the first 3 who gave poor ratings saw but I enjoyed my experience at this place. The food reminds me of mom's cooking. The server was experienced and knew what she was talking about. I ordered the springs rolls as a starter. The rolls were nice full of crispy vegetables and a good slice of shrimp and pork. The sauce is good but as most places it could be spicier. The main course was a grilled pork chop with the Vietnamese omelet with rice. The rice was cooked perfectly, the pork chop was seasoned well and cooked perfectly. Most Vietnamese restaurants the pork chop would be par cooked and then fried. Not this place. This cook this to order. The chop was a nice cut and was cut to prevent the chop from curling up. The fish sauce that comes with the meal was not bad. Usually it would be under seasoned and not as spicy. The end of the meal ended with a sample of bread pudding which was good but served cold. The strawberry cake was great but a little dry. The baker/ owner was aware of this. Overall the service and food was good. I would come back. Once again I'm not sure what the other low reviews were seeing and talking about. The owners came out to the table to welcome us to the restaurant and I spoke about the food and experience to them. They took it well and I would not be surprised to see improvements

text: I've been wanting to try the Bleeding Deacon for some time. I finally visited this weekend. Upon entering, this place screams rockabilly dive-bar. Super dim lights, tattoed bartenders, menus made out of album sleeves. At first impression I felt like this was going to be a new fav of mine. I entered and there wasn't a table. There really isn't anyone to direct or greet you. After a bit of time one of the bartenders noticed me and asked if we were waiting for a table. She took my name and drink order and wrote my name down on a wait sheet behind the bar. 15 minutes later, my table was ready. I attempted to close my tab but it took over 10 minutes to do so. I think I was there during shift change because at the time there were 3 bartenders. After I gave my money to one, I waited and waited for my change and credit card... I gave it to them to open a tab. Nobody came back. After some frustration, one of them looked at me and remembered they owed me a returned card and change. The menu is interesting. Typical bar food, but with a bit of flair. However, I have to thank this place for being the first time I've ever had to use a flashlight to see the menu. I see the elderly do this all the time and get a chuckle out of it, I was humbled when I had to use my phone to light up my menu here. In the back of the place there simply isn't enought light to see. I started with the truffle fries. They were very good. Then on to split a burger and fish tacos. The tacos were on stale hard tortillas and were nothing more than fried fish with a little sauce. The burger was super charred. It tasted like it was scraped from the bottom of a BBQ pit. I like a bit of charring, but this was a bit much. Both dishes sucked. I took a picture of my food. It was the only time I was able to see it since my phone has a flash with the camera. Service was average. I really enjoy divey places. But if the food sucks, and bar service was poor, why would I ever come back?

text: Quick and dirty: They ripped me off charging me 2xs for parking. When I tried to get my money back, the man I was dealing with who takes the money in the window said "It wasn't his fault I paid twice." text: I rented with JMH Realty for 7 years (2 different apartments), and both my experiences were great. Alan Folkman and his team are extremely well-organized, efficient and reliable. The entire team is very responsive to any issues or concerns I needed addressed--I usually received a response within a few hours to questions or concerns (even outside of business hours). I only had a couple of minor issues in the apartment, both of which were fixed within 1-2 business days. In addition, if I had any special requests, Alan would not only inform me upfront of any costs for using their services, but also made sure to give me ideas for cheaper options that I could do myself. My only complaint is that the women in the front office can be pretty curt, but you really only have to deal with them in the initial few days while signing the lease. Plus it's the nature of the realty business in a busy city like Philly, and in my opinion, efficiency counts for a lot more. I must also say that they got a lot friendlier after the lease was signed and you became a tenant. All of the paperwork was done on time and the whole process of lease signing etc. was very organized. You also receive regular updates by email about trash-pickup (in case of holidays and changed dates), ways to conserve electricity/heat, and other helpful tips like controlling for bed bugs etc. Alan himself is great. He genuinely cares and tries to make your stay as comfortable as possible. For the second apartment I rented, the owner (who was using JMH for property management services) turned out to be an abrasive and rude man, but I was very glad to not have to deal with him, and only deal with Alan and the JMH team--that made things a lot more convenient and my life a lot simpler, which speaks to the importance of having a good realty company who know what they're doing and do it well. Even after I moved out of the apartment, everything was done promptly. My questions and concerns were answered as quickly as they were while I was a tenant, Alan offered to provide a reference for my future landlords, and I received almost my entire security deposit back (whatever little was not returned was reasonable). I've now moved to the suburbs, but if I ever move back into Philadelphia, I'm sure I'll be going back to JMH.

text: Stopped by for a late sandwich for supper, and got there after they had closed the kitchen and the cook was leaving. Christina, who was still manning the counter, was most kind and quickly offered up Bayshore Breeze's Cuban sandwich as a good alternative. After eating this great Cuban, I think the Food Gods worked out my good fortune. Bayshore Breeze Market & Grill is located inside a very nice gas station/market right on the corner of corner of Alt. 19 and Curlew/Causeway Blvd. This intersection is directly at the entrance to the causeway to Honeymoon/Caladesi Island State Parks, and couldn't be more convenient to grab your food/drinks for a nice day at the beach. There are about a half dozen tables available for dining-in, and the entire area is very clean and neat. While they have a nice supply of prepared Cubans for serving customers quickly, I ordered mine with a twist, and Christina gladly obliged my custom order in spite of the late hour. You can't ask for better service than that. Bayshore Breeze's Cubans are not for the faint of heart. This is no wimpy sandwich. Just picking it up lets you know this thing is absolutely packed with meat, which by the way is filled with hand-pulled roast pork that the owner marinates for 24 hours in mojo, then is slow-roasted for another 7-8 hours before serving. None of that generic/store-bought sliced pork here at all, and the result elevates this Cuban far above most of it's competitors. Add in thinly-sliced ham and cheese, then tasty cuban bread hot-pressed to a perfect crust, and you've got Cuban heaven. And if you need any more to convince to check Bayshore Breeze out, go to their website and you'll find a list of online specials. They have multiple coupons which you can print out and present for breakfast/lunch/dinner/chicken pita/side order/frozen yogurt, and get one at half-price for every one you order. Even better, the daily specials page (accessible from the coupon page) lists a variety of different weekday "buy one, get one free" sandwich specials available from 3pm to closing. text: I had an excellent dining experience here on 08-25-2011. Maximo's always had a good reputation, but I had not eaten here in 20 years, so I wasn't quite sure what to expect. We arrived at 7:00 pm on a Thursday, and the place was pretty empty. We had reservations but were told we could sit wherever we wanted. We opted for the very first booth (2-top) situated on the left wall as you walk in. We were seated immediately and greated by our server (Erin). Our drinks arrived in a jiffy, along with some delicious hot bread. The restaurant is narrow but you don't get the feeling like you're sitting right on top of the table next to you. The decor is upscale and the stained wooden ceilings are a nice touch. There are pictures everywhere but they don't take away from the dining experience. For an appetizer, we had the Sicilian shrimp which was grilled and wrapped in prosciutto. They give you four nice sized prawns, so it's worth the money. My entree selection was the Osso Buco, which is a veal shank cooked on the bone. It is the house specialty and is absolutely delicious. You don't need a knife because the veal is so tender than you can eat it with a fork. As is customary, they give you a tiny appetizer fork so that you can eat the marrow from inside the bone. I know this may sound a little weird to some, but don't knock it till you try it. Although not as tasty as the veal itself, the marrow was very rich and had a buttery texture. We also had the fire roaseted seafood entree, which consisted of gulf shrimp, large scallops and fish (grouper). I love scallops and shrimp, but the grouper stole the show on this plate. The habernero infused olive oil really kicks it up a notch, but not to the point where you don't taste the seafood and appreciate it for what it is. For dessert, we had the tiramisu beacuse it's made in house and it doesn't get any fresher than that. Although not my favorite dessert, I prefer in house desserts to those that are store bought or shipped to the restaurant. Lastly, I'd like to commend my server Erin. She was extremly attentive (without being intrusive) and very helpful with the menu choices. Her personality make her perfectly suited for her job and she is a definite asset to Maximo's. It's readily apparent when a person truly enjoys their job and Erin fits the bill. Thanks for making our dining experience here a memorable one.

So we went down after 10pm; plenty of empty tables which is good, but a lot of them were dirty. Yuck! Overall the food was okay. Mom had the French onion soup and a small salad. My sister had the grilled chicken with mashed potatoes. I had a grilled cheese sandwich with just white cheddar which came with a tomato soup. My brother got the penne marinara. I just want to say that the marinara was more likely an arrabiata sauce. But we did eat. It took forever for my brother to get any extra parmasean cheese. By the time he did get it, he was done eating (not to say that he completed the food). Also, we were given no warning about the kitchen closing, so we couldn't get dessert. It would have been nice if the waitress had given us a little heads up. She said the kitchen closed at 12am; it wasn't 12am yet. Whatever. Now, about the Cafe Los Arcos... We ate there every morning because we were given vouchers and wouldn't have to pay for the buffet. So for 3 out of 4 days there was an omelet station. Great! Each day was a different guy. On the fourth day he was no where to be seen but I was told to just order my omelet with the server. Fine. Let me just say, that there is something about seeing your food cooked in front of you versus having it brought out. So I guess I'd say the first 3 days were the better tasting omelets. The service was alright. The first 3 days they were on top of it. I don't know if it was the timing on the fourth day, or what. The absence of the omelet guy and our decision that it'd be nice to dine "al fresco" for once, it was not such a great morning. Anyway, there wan't a big selection of breads. Just these mini fake bagels. The potatoes were lackluster. They used the wrong kind of potatoes for "breakfast potatoes." The French toast was fine. Nothing to write home about. That was pretty much my breakfast for four days, though. I looked at the oatmeal which freaked me out. Bleh. I don't eat lox or bacon/sausage but they had those. Danishes, croissants, cheeses, "bread pudding," cereals. So there were choices. I'm just glad that we didn't have to pay for this overpriced spread, because I'm sure there are other places in Santa Barbara with better breakfast options for much cheaper.
label: NEG

text: It's been one of my (many) guilty pleasures in New Orleans since my college days at Tulane in the 1980s ... so I've had plenty of snoballs from Plum Street! I don't dish out 5 stars unless it's a place that I would request a "last meal" from, so believe me when I say that it's worthy! The "small pail" is probably big enough for most appetites, but if you're going for anything larger, beware of brain freeze! There are also kids sizes, yet I've never met a kid in New Orleans that isn't already at professional snoball eater/slurper/sucker so they will handle a larger size with no problem. If it's your first time EVER trying a New Orleans "snoball," I would suggest the basic and probably most-popular flavors: Strawberry, Ice Cream, Bubble Gum, Spearmint, Nectar, or Chocolate (made with REAL Hershey's Chocolate Syrup). But there are plenty more flavors, so if you can't decide, ask for 1/2 & 1/2 ... or just plan a return trip!

text: This is everything a french-nola-noveau restaurant should be (not to say there are many). It is elegant but relaxed. The decor is very stylish but at the same time cozy. The staff is very professional to say the least with an impeccable knowledge of every plate and how it's made. And finally the food... John Besh takes his creativity and detail to a different level of complexity; superb! If you want to go out to in New Orleans and have a very nice evening with amazing food, this is the place to go. First we started with a Amuse bouche wonderfully plated inside an egg shell. Its a delicate custard infused with seafood broth and topped with a brioche and caviar. As appetizer i had the Gnocchi with Crab and Black Truffles which was excellent. It was creamy and rich in flavor but the texture of the Gnocchi (little clouds) was so delicate it's even hard to describe. For the main course i had Pork Belly which was done to perfection. It was infused with a delicate broth. The pork belly was sitting on a bed of greens that just gave more depth to an already superb dish. I had the intention to photograph every plate but i was so mesmerized with the presentation and smell that i totally forgot. For desert I had the Napoleon of Nougatine with Valhrona chocolate bavarois and salted toffee ice-cream which was out of this world. I would have had two of these but we had to catch the flight back to Miami. Sommelier Michelle Gueydan's wine list is impressive with a wide variety of selections in the $100+ range and some lower price option that are great. We had a Taft Street Zin 2007 from the Russian River. One of the best meals I've ever had.
label: POS

text: A group of us ended up here for the sole purpose of happy hour at 5:30 in the evening and 1) they had no "happy hour" and 2) their seating requirements were confusing. The staff said that we would not receive any "waitstaff service where we were sitting." Wha? We were sitting in the best seats in the house: alfresco next to the tres-expensive-looking heat lamps and iconic La Arcada fountain. So let me stop right here: the "fancy" seating where you could get "wait staff" service was in a claustrophobic tent -- huh? It's Santa Barbara -- you can sit outside all day long and all night long with the proper heat lamp. This tent thing looked like something out of the Revolutionary War. I was expecting Florence Nightingale to emerge any minute. Okay, so we were an easy-going bunch, and continued to hand-carry our own drinks out to the BEST SEAT IN THE HOUSE that wasn't in a claustrophobic tent, and for TWO HOURS, yes, I do not exaggerate -- TWO HOURS -- the waitstaff refused to clear our empty drink glasses as we continued to purchase drink after drink. (I know what you're thinking, we were a group of drunk banshees that the waitstaff was trying to avoid -- yes, drunkards, but no, not banshees, and not uncivil in any way. In fact we were all local career-ladies willing to pay out the $$$ for drinks.) At hour three we couldn't take it anymore. (Note: We stayed because it was a glorious S.B. night and loved the fact that we had a great outdoor table.) We asked a passing wait staff member if we could get service at our table. She replied, "Oh, we thought you were wrapping it up." Wrapping it up for two hours as we continued to order our own drinks at the bar and bring them back to a table amidst a bunch of refuse that the wait staff refused to clear? Tee hee -- um, no. At that point we became *very special* and everything was cleared and taken care of. Too little, too late. (Side note: All wait staff were very accommodating and friendly within their context of the bar and hostess area. No offense to them BUT...) C'mon Cielito -- you claim to be bringing back an S.B. tradition, but the only S.B. tradition I want to come back is friendly service, uncomplicated seating under the stars, and a good time. Oh, and maybe let someone ride in on a horse during Fiesta. That is all.

text: I'm hesitant to review places where I don't live, but over the course of this week, I've come here enough times to lose count. It's an oasis from the neon lights and heavy food of the French Quarter: perfectly made espresso drinks, locally baked sweets, light meals (sandwiches, crepes, salads) under $10, free wi-fi, and a bright, clean modern aesthetic. It honestly had me wishing I lived in New Orleans, so it could become my coffeeshop of choice. Miscellaneous useful things to know: - The hours are 7am to 8pm. - They will soon get their beverage license and become a wine bar as well (the "grapes" part of their motto). - The crepes are cooked to a crispy brown, instead of a soft beige; it makes eating them with a knife and fork tricky, but adds nice textural contrast. - They're very happy to make custom espresso drinks. This morning I went wild with a honey-hazelnut-cinnamon latte, and it was perfectly balanced. - The side salad that comes with their sandwiches is shockingly good in its purity: chopped romaine, a thin vinaigrette with plenty of pepper and vinegar, and a sprinkling of parmesan. It's been open a few weeks, and it's usually not very crowded, so I really hope that they find the strong customer base that they completely deserve. An easy 5 stars.

text: I have been here a few times, and keep waiting for the other shoe to drop. There is NO WAY that a place in Nola can be this perfect. No way. However, I am starting to believe that there is no other shoe... This place is perfect. I heard about this place having vegan food awhile ago via yelp, and checked it out on a Saturday afternoon. I got the vegan rico, a mock meat sandwich to go, and some fresh juice. I have since been back for several other items, but haven't tried everything yet. I said YET. The vegan "pork" was amazing. Seriously, it puts every mock meat I have purchased/made to shame. I don't know how they did it. I'm wagering that it's ground up unicorn and magic dust. The dressing complimented the light greens, diaya cheese, and perfectly prepared plantain. I also had a slice of banana cake, and i thought i was going to implode, it was banana-licioua. The staff is just as wonderful as the food. The owners are both extremely friendly and knowledgeable about vegan options and Brazillian food. The other staff are awesome, always happy to see me, and clearly love their jobs. That, my yelpy friends, is a rarity in any city, especially New Orleans! The specials sound delicious, and I get them through facebook (or the analog way: the board outside the restaurant). Their soups are inventive, which will be nice when winter rolls around! Apparently dinner hours are coming SOON, and I can't wait!!! I will be a regular here for sure!! Thank you, Carmo, for showing me that delicious, elegant, and beautiful vegan food IS possible in New Orleans!

Three of us had chicken fajitas that arrived charred with a small container of tiny tortillas to share. We were assured that the tortillas were bottomless but we felt like Oliver Twist when we asked for more. The hamburger was delivered looked good and it was BIG. Be prepared. The Santa Fe chicken salad also elicited no complaints. I can't comment on the desserts because we had baked a cake that afternoon and we all had coffee and cake in the peace and quiet of our home. The service is slow, which may be why the fajitas came out charred. The servers guard their territory like junkyard dogs so you can only deal with problems with your particular server. Perhaps service is better on a weekday but I wouldn't bet on it. Chili's is run by a generic corporation called Brinker International that seems more interested in selling Franchises and cellphone apps than in improving the food or service. Unlike Arnold, I won't be back

text: I've been jonesing for a hot fudge sundae for months. You know, tall glass, ice cream, fudge, more ice cream, more fudge, crushed peanuts, whipped cream and a cherry on top? I've never been here before and didn't know what to expect but I've heard great things about it. Upon arriving and see the little line out side the small shop, I know that I've come to the right place. There are about 15 table lining up outside the small corner stores with trash "barrels" and metal tubs for dirty dishes. Inside, it is decided colonial with servers dressing up down to the fan drapes made out of flags that lines the walls. An old-timey cashier that made clinky sound. I do enjoy these things. I originally just want a sundae, but the boyfriend wanted an ice cream soda... so I got them both! I ordered a coke soda with coconut ice cream and a Southern Sympathizer with hydro cookies and peanut butter ice cream. I have to say I've never got into ice cream sodas, I think it's a waste of ice cream and a waste on soda. I like ice cream too much to see it melt away in soda and I've never been a big fan of creamy sodas but at the end it wasn't so bad. Don't try to put your spoon in the soda when it first come out. I did and it overflowed and splashed all over. The Southern Sympathizer was sprinkled with pecan and brittles with caramel sauce and whipped cream. The ice cream was really good but it turned out a bit sweet. With no glass of water for relief and a faucet to wash my hands, it is a bit inconvenient but how can you not have fun with ice cream? Next time I'll have a bottle of water ready. P.S. This is a cash only place, the things here are about $10 a piece and I nearly not have enough cash, so make sure before coming.

text: I waited with eager anticipation all spring and summer as I watched board after board be applied to the exterior of this building. I would dream away the hours envisioning bringing friends to my new favorite hang out where we would laugh over beers and fried chicken & waffles. Sadly, I shall have to take my friends elsewhere as both visits I've made have left me feeling disappointed. After Visit #1, I figured they needed to work out the kinks. Visit #2 (a month later) was no better. On both visits I ordered appetizers not wanting to invest in a full meal if the apps weren't good. Visit #1: The poor hostess looked like there was a fire somewhere. She was out of breath and disheveled. However, I saw no smoke and the restaurant was hardly busy. Regardless, we were seated and left to sit there for nearly 10 minutes. Our server finally popped over and asked if we knew what we wanted not realizing we hadn't been given menus. After sitting for another 5 and on our way to a movie, we decided to play it safe and just order a couple beers and the sausage platter. It boasted 3 types of sausage and assorted cheese. The server didn't know which sausage was which because she's a vegetarian. :-/ They all looked and tasted the same to me though: dry. Sharing the plate with these was a ball (and I mean, baseball) of bleu/blue cheese. I guess that's "assorted". Served with the burnt bits and planet size cheese ball was an assortment of mustard (yum but probably store bought) and a few pieces of pretzel bread. The bread and the mustard were the highlight. Visit #2: Same hostess, same panic, even fewer patrons. Ordered the soup of the day (Seafood Cioppino) and sliders. Soup was flavorful but basic like seafood stock and tomato sauce stirred together. No real depth. I was hoping it would come out with some tasty pretzel bread (since everything there is served on/with it) so I could sop of the leftover soup but nah. The sliders were a big disappointment. All 3 were cold and not just lukewarm but cold. The beef was so cold that I couldn't eat it. Pork on the other hand had enough flavor that I didn't mind it seemed straight out of the cooler. The highlight of this visit was our server. She was super nice and apologized that our food took a little long to come out. I'm wrapping up this review with a pout. I so wanted this to be a great spot to hang out, nibble and watch football. Maybe I'll give it another month or so and try again but, in the meantime, I won't be going or recommending or dreaming of it. :(

text: When I was in High School one of my best friends lived across from a pretty ugly vacant lot. An old hotel (the El Mirasol) had been torn down many years before. The lot was full of old tires, weeds higher than our heads and a stray appliance or two. It was a great old lot! We loved that lot as much as any teenage boys can love a vacant lot. It was also the home to one of Santa Barbara's greatest transformations! It is now a botanical wonderland. When my wife and I picked varieties for our landscaping, it is where we went. It has a creek and a pond. There are Koi fish and Turtles (lots of turtles) it even had some piranahs for a period--seriously! There are hundreds of varieties of non-native plants, if you have an interest in things botanical, you will be in heaven! From what I hear some people actually like to do things other than wine taste in this town. The story behind it is wonderful. When it was dedicated the donor was anonymous. When that person died, her name was revealed. Alice Keck Park (her father founded Standard Oil Co.) Her name presented a problem in naming the place. Alice Keck Park park. Hmmm didn't have a great ring to it... so park was changed to memorial gardens and all was good. I have been in the park when bands were playing when people practiced their juggling! It is active and fun. There are paths and places to picnic. Certainly a great, great jewel in this wonderful town! If you would like to learn more about this wonderful little oasis... here is a link to a nice article: http://www.independent.com/news/2006/jun/08/the-story-of-alice-keck-park-m/

text: well, i guess i will be the first one to rain on the parade. i am no beer expert, snob or anything other than someone who has been enjoying beer for the past 25 or so years. i like stroh's and miller high life and i also like good porters, ipa's and other craft and imported beers. i have had many friends get into home brewing and most of them started with a $120 all extract kit that they got for a birthday or christmas- the beer at fat bottom reminds me of the first attempt by these first timers. thin, shallow, watery, artificial tasting when the addition of smoke or coffee flavorings, several of the beers tasted only slightly different. believe me i wanted to like this place since it is only blocks from my house- but i just can't. when i walked into the brewery (through the actual brewing area- cool way to enter a brewery for sure) it smelled like nothing- none of the smells you get blanketed in at every other brewery i have ever been in. that was an indicator of what was to come. i did see a sign for a porter which is my favorite fall/early winter beer. instantly i wanted that to start. it is a nice place and i hear the food is quite good. i didn't eat there so i cannot comment on that. the interior is a slightly different take on the beaten to death barn wood look that is taking over the restaurant scene- it's nice for sure but on the tail end of the rustic trend. the tables were made out of planks of wood/trees and the surface of our table was not level (the natural contour of the tree) and there were certain places we couldn't put our beers. neat looking but not a practical choice. another personal pet peeve is when the music from the kitchen is competing with the volume of the music in the dining/drinking area. jazz vocalists in the dining area and some hip pop blasting from the kitchen. that is easy to fix. now on to the bigger problem- the beer. we decided to order the tasting and the black beer was out of stock but we tried the rest of them. the first 3 lighter beers tasted pretty much the same sharing the same unremarkable features and flavors. i was excited to taste the porter but was smacked with the smell of coffee. i know porters and i know they can have hints of coffee in them but this porter smelled like a cup of coffee. after taking a sip the flavor matched the smell. pure coffee with a hint of beer- maybe. porters are beers of body and rich flavor and this porter was as thin as the light beers (all the beers had the same watery body and flavor). i remember one of the beers having the taste of way too much artificial smoke flavoring. we were there early and were waited on by nice people in a timely manner but the hospitality was smashed by the low quality of the beer. maybe it is a new breed of craft/micro brewery for people who think guinness is gross. i really want to like this place and if i based it on neat interior and friendly staff instead of sure spill tables and awful beer i would like it. i really really really cannot believe the beer at this place is not getting a total online reaming from nashville's beer lovers. the beer truly is not good. when 2 people share a sampling of six 4oz pours and each of the glasses is more than half full when the bill is paid THAT AIN'T GOOD. the porter and the stout were not drinkable and the others were a half step ahead of those. get some consultation, a new and more experienced/knowledgable/talented brewer, make sure your recipes are written down correctly, taste your beers against other similar styled beers and take notes, get some help of some variety- something. i know opening a new restaurant or brewery is a huge undertaking and i salute them for getting this far but if your business is based around beer at least make it drinkable. i want this place to make it and i cheer for them as i sit somewhere else and drink a beer and wait for them to work the colony of bugs out of their system. i know i sound like a typical online critic who is too hard on a new place but these are serious issues for this place and they need to be addressed. if i didn't care i would have just written 'it sucked' (or nothing at all) but i care and i hope someone from fat bottom reads this and takes note. the word on the 'beer' street about this place is very similar to what i have written- it's an 'also ran.' maybe business is booming with the quality of beer they are serving and has an audience in nashville. if so- carry on but it's a mystery to me but not a compelling enough mystery to seek an answer to. if you are into the look and feel of a brewery with a beer garden and don't want to be bothered by bold and full flavored beers this is your go to place.

text: I have only been here a handful of times, and I need to visit more often. The fare is rooted in French and Belgian cuisine with an American twist, and it's delicious. The downstairs area is casual and cozy with the upstairs having more of a sports bar vibe. Brugge is great for three things: mussels, beer, and fries. The impressive selection of moules frites (mussels) is accompanied by varying sauces which everyone should try; especially the Provencal sauce. If bivalves aren't your thing, then choose from the assorted sandwiches and dinner crepes. Main courses aside, one should never leave Brugge without having some fries and some beer. The fries are great by themselves, but you should make some selections from the menagerie of tasty dipping sauces. Good beer is a highly subjective topic, so I cannot advise which is best nor would I attempt to do so. However, the Triple de Ripple is my favorite. Alas, the establishment strictly enforces its two drink maximum for this beer due to its potency. If your hunger is not completely obliterated after your meal, then order a dessert crepe. Once you leave Brugge, the only indulgence you will be wanting is a cigarette.
label: POS

text: I never write online reviews but felt like I had to after my most recent trip to Pep Boys. I have always felt like this location is a little pushy and overpriced but I was in a pinch for a car inspection and oil change so I figured it would be fine to take it there. Everything seemed to go fine and they finished everything up in a somewhat timely manner (an hour and a half) and then the typical suggested services started. I normally turn all these down but they mentioned corrosion on the battery and a simple service to remove it and help save the battery life, 10 minutes, $10, easy fix so I agreed to it. I left Pep Boys alright with the cost and service and headed to the next shopping center over on my way home. When I got back in my car, the battery was dead. I called Pep Boys back and they came over to give me a jump and I brought my car back to them to take a look at it. They then told me that the battery was bad and I needed to get a new one. In any other circumstances I wouldn't have been that surprised because my car is around the age where I might need a new battery but it seems like an awfully big coincidence that not even 10 minutes after I have service done on my previously normally functioning battery, I now am back at Pep Boys shelling out another $100 for a new battery. I will say I appreciated them coming out and jumping my car. As I said, I have always been leery of Pep Boys in the past and this just solidified my feelings. I won't be going back to Pep Boys anytime in the near future.

text: Sbraga was the restaurant my boyfriend selected for his birthday dinner. I had been anxious to get back since our first visit in December, and when I checked out the current menu I was even more stoked. We went all out and opted for the beverage pairing, but I started things off with a glass of sangria, which was super fruity and flavorful. The first course really set the bar high. Housemade mozzarella with local tomatoes and fried clams appealed to all my Jersey girl senses. This was the perfect summer dish. Next up was parsley risotto with escargot and prosciutto. I love Sbraga's risotto. Art raved over his scallop and pork belly, but the plate that got the most attention was the tempura fried lobster tail that was sent out from the kitchen. Lobster has never been more tender. At this point we were feeling pretty full and it was only halfway through the meal. Fortunately, the third course was presented in a smaller portion. My plate consisted of barbecue chicken confit, pickles, cole slaw and onion rings. Tasty and fun. The dessert course at Sbraga is not an afterthought, but a vital part of the meal. I wasn't walking out of there without the mascarpone/coffee granita dessert from my previous visit, which was thankfully still on the menu. The boyfriend opted for a cherry coke dessert that was totally unique and really well executed. The kitchen sent out the strawberry rhubarb streusal, which was served hot with a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top. So delish. Our second Sbraga visit was really pretty flawless. Service was excellent and everyone seemed to be working in harmony. The restaurant was also packed, which was awesome to see. I'm looking forward to our next visit, most likely after the menu changes up yet again!
label: POS

They are located in Seminole Heights area, which is the new hipster area of Tampa, but they have been here long before that. They have a sit in and take out options. Their green hot sauce is out of this world. Be warned: if you are considering other properties, take it from a former Tampa Bay resident of eight years, please go to those. They put about $26 million dollars into the common areas - two restaurants and a lobby area. Yes, attractive. They should have put that into the lodges. The suites are something straight out of a Golden Girls episode. The rooms are a bit musty as well. *Getting anywhere you need to go and requiring a shuttle to get there-very inconvenient. (However, this isn't a complaint as this is a resort and they are set up that way. Rather, it's a warning to those who don't want to have to rely on shuttles to get anywhere). *The largest pool, The Loch Ness, was closed early on a weekend day for a private party. It was nice, definitely NOT quiet nor peaceful. Very child-friendly. So we went to a smaller pool because of the early closing. Eh. It was ok. Small, indeed. The service was horrible at the cafe' located at the Loch Ness pool. I asked the guy for a smoothie and he looked at me liked I asked him to go to China for sushi. We had brought our towels with us from Loch Ness to the Copperhead pool and everyone asked us where we got them. Apparently they weren't providing towels at other pools. *The one highlight of the entire resort is the Osprey restaurant and our server Daniel. Each night the meals were quite good and Daniel was excellent. Packard's, the steak restaurant was also good. A bit stuffier, but good all the same. There was an unfortunate incident with one of the meeting attendees having glass in her meal. *The overall service was extremely poor. Despite knowing our group was coming, the staff was completely unprepared. Approximately fifty of our attendees waited hours for their room keys - after normal check-in time and were offered no refreshments or words other than "it'll be a few minutes and housekeeping doesn't have your room ready yet." Another attendee got to his room and it hadn't even been made up. The bed linens were not even changed. *The meeting space is ample, however, it's dank and musty. Overall the only reason you'd go there is to golf. And eat. And golf some more. So I suppose that for people who actually golf this place could work. text: I wish I could give this place a better review...I really do. But after the latest fiasco, I am overall very disappointed with my experience at this hotel. But there were other staff and billing problems that led me to leave this review. The problems first started when I checked-in, and was given my room key, etc. The room I went to was already occupied by someone else. Luckily, it was someone I knew (we were all traveling on business together), so there wasn't a huge issue there. They moved me to another room. Due to the "double booking" of the rooms, they offered me complimentary cheese and wine, and said it would be right up. Well, I waited and waited for as long as I could (I had dinner plans, so I couldn't wait all night!), and I tried calling the front desk, who transferred me to room service, and no one from room service ever picked up - so I gave up. Upon leaving for dinner, I mentioned this to the manager, who apologized and promised there would be complimentary cookies and beverages in my room when I returned. When I returned, there were not any cookies to be found. I went downstairs for a drink with my coworker, and we went to the front desk afterwards to inquire about the situation. They told me they weren't aware of the "arrangement" but they did inform me that they were out of cookies.... Well, when I finally went up to my room that night - surprise! There was cake! And the cheese and wine! I thought things were FINALLY looking up! But the next morning, my bill came under the door - they had me checking out that day, when I actually was staying there another day. I had to go to the front desk, and have the entire situation sorted out - which it was sorted out, but at this point, I felt like I had spent too much time bringing all of these problems to their attention! After I finally checked out the following day, I thought my problems with this hotel were over - until I saw that they overcharged my credit card by $106!!! What's worse, is that when I noticed the discrepancy, I called the hotel, was transferred, and left a message that was not returned. I then called again (which I should not have to do - I would hope it would be them following up!!!), at which point I finally talked to someone, who told me that my credit card was charged the amount that someone else's card was meant to be charged - they mixed up our credit cards! Quite honestly, this created a hassle for submitting my expense report at work - and between the other problems I've mentioned, the fire alarm going off endlessly one night (scared the crap out of me - I see this happened to several others who left reviews, which doesn't make me hopeful that they're trying to fix the problem), and the "dusty" feel to the rooms, I don't think I'll stay here again.

text: As a fellow Yelper stated in his review, if I was writing a review based upon the food alone, I would give it four stars, maybe even five. The rolls are inventive and tasty. I like the spicy Sex and the City roll, and the flaming Oh My God roll isn't just fun to look at it, it tastes great too. I am a Philly roll junky, and whenever I eat at a sushi restaurant, I have to order one. Tani's Philly doesn't disappoint. The Miami roll (I believe that's what it is called) is awesome! It is a fried Philly roll, so come on, you can't go wrong there. Now, why is Tani only receiving two stars, you ask? Well, the service is SO BAD that even if I were dining at Nobu, I still wouldn't want to come back. I know one of the servers who used to work there, and the one time I had the pleasure of having him as my server, I had an excellent time. Every other server acts like I'm inconveniencing them by placing a drink order and (gasp!) that I may want to order some food sometime during the evening. Ballsy of me, no? If you've read some of my other reviews, you know that I was in the restaurant industry for 7 years, 5 of them as a server. If a busy server forgets to refill my drink or takes a little time to approach my table, I'm fine with that. I understand "being in the weeds". But it is not okay to approach a table with a look on your face that says "it's YOUR fault I'm running behind and stressed". On several occasions, I've come extremely close to saying something along the lines of "you work in a sushi restaurant... in Clayton... on a Saturday night, you're going to be busy, get over it". My biggest overall issue with the service is that servers will drop the sushi off at your table, say the names of the rolls so quickly that you have NO idea what is in front of you, and then sprint away not even stopping to ask if anyone needs a refill. It takes a lot for me to tip under 20%. I mean, a LOT. The fact that I have had no problem tipping 15-17% scares me. I really wish the service was even half as good as the food. If that were the case, I'd be a regular at Tani, no questions asked.

text: My husband and I are from Austin, so we really love Texas BBQ. We're not really experts in pulled pork or deep south BBQ. We were really intrigued when we found this place, which is only a minute away from where we live. We shared their 2 meat combo platter and got the baby back ribs and the sliced brisket with the carolina sauce, plus the sweet potato fries and cole slaw, which came out to a little under $15. The store layout is similar to a local pizza joint-- not a good place to eat in IMO (although there are tables and chairs) but great for takeout. I read an article they had hanging on their wall about the restaurant, and it said that Fletcher's was a restaurant that featured a sampling of all different types of BBQ- brisket from Texas, plus ribs and pulled pork from other parts of the south. They also have several types of sauce-- again, one Texas-inspired, another carolina, and a third that I don't remember. It's family-run by a family that decided to pursue their dreams away from corporate America. I'm always excited to try out local businesses. They said that they had been open for about 2 years. Being from Texas, I had a few expectations of what a BBQ place should be like, but it could just be that people do BBQ differently in different places. The menu features chopped and sliced brisket, ribs, pulled pork and pulled chicken, plus a few other things like a smoked whole or half chicken. Interestingly, they don't have any sausage, which to me should be a staple. Their sides are also a mix of different places-- cole slaw, sweet potato fries, collard greens, tater tots, mac and cheese, and baked beans.... but no potato salad, which again is a staple down in Texas. The thing that bugged me the most was that there was no sweet tea to be found, but I'd rather take a place with no sweet tea and great BBQ than a place with bad BBQ and great sweet tea. No free side items like pickles or onions were available either. The brisket was sliced generously, and not thinly. it's wasn't melt-in-your-mouth but it wasn't super chewy either. My favorite part was that it wasn't too charred on the outside but had nice darkness to it. The baby back ribs are fall-off-the-bone. I can see why the ribs got rave reviews from other yelpers. I wish there was more sauce on the meat, but that's probably a personal preference, as I'm used to there being extra tubs of sauce to dunk your meat in as opposed to the sauce only being poured directly onto the meat. I really liked that the meat was served on top of a delicious buttered piece of Texas toast. Delicious! I'm so glad to find a place that does BBQ well right here in Abington and that I don't need to drive 1600 miles to get it. It's not pure Texas BBQ but both my husband and I really enjoyed our meal. We'll be back, and next time we'll try the pulled pork and some different sides!

We were greeted instantly and seated right away. Here's the skinny on what we ordered: - Crawfish omelette. Has brie cheese, avocado, and crawfish of course! Everything was really fresh and I thought the flavors went really well together! It's a simple dish, and nothing overpowers the crawfish. - Corned beef hash. Big chunks of corned beef topped with 2 sunny side up eggs.. and a side of either toast or a biscuit. (see my photos) Surrey's is my favorite breakfast place in NOLA so far! I love that they have healthier options (they have vegan and vegetarian options as well!).. they even kale juice and their juices are made fresh too! The downside? It's cash only!

text: I love the charm and character of independent local businesses. What drives me crazy, though, is when that independent nature also comes with massive inconsistency. I've had great bagels from Spread, and awesome bagels from Spread. I stayed away for a while because of the prices and the lines, but gave them another shot this past weekend. Had a whole-wheat everything with a healthy dollop of Amish Farm Cream Cheese, and it made for a fantastic breakfast in Rittenhouse Square. It was a bit less toasted than I would normally prefer, but still really tasty. Went back this morning for the same thing, only to get home and find a charred bagel with a modicum of cream cheese on only half the bagel. The result was dry, smoky, and a waste. I'm willing to pay the higher-than-average prices if I know I'm going to get something great. I just don't have that confidence here.

The location was great, and the price was definitely right. I cooked my own meals in the kitchen, and enjoyed the view from the 16th floor. The Wi-Fi is free, but I found it to be spotty and finicky, and the kitchen in my suite could have had more dishes to cook with. That said, the room was huge, really clean, and well-appointed. The renovated rooms are tres cute! I feel like I got a great deal for my money, and I will definitely stay here again if I need a room in Philadelphia. Ask at the desk to make sure you get a renovated room, and you'll be very happy here!

text: The post-Katrina rendition of MSY is a huge improvement over the gloomy, dingy and crowded prior airport. Everywhere you turn the vibe is one of being somewhere else; at a business function, drinking Hurricanes in the French Quarter or on a flight back home. text: Whoever described the ambiance as "divey" was spot on! What a hidden gem off the well (b)eaten path of the surrounding St. Charles area. A few of us came here for a friend's birthday. We initially started off at the bar. They had some good specials and nice beers on tap. The Tchoupitoulas IPA was a perfect way for me to end the day. Imagine my surprise when a small door above the bar opened and a lady popped out bearing po-boys for the dudes at the bar next to us! I thought I had just stumbled into the New Orlean's version of the Keebler elf cookie tree. We took our beers upstairs. I kinda wish they brought the cool vibe of the downstairs bar to the upstairs... since the decor is seriously lacking up there. Ordering is super informal, with the cooks also taking the cash/orders and then cooking it. Our large order came out a bit slowly, but we were having a good time and so didn't mind waiting. Specials were up on the board next to the little food ordering window. Friends that had the highly recommended roast beef po-boys were not disappointed. We all also tried the friend onion rings (not what I'm used to, but delicious nonetheless) and the friend macaroni and cheese (recommended by the cooks). Ok, I'm not normally a fan of friend mac 'n cheese, but it was delicious! Perfectly fried on the outside and warm/gooey on the inside. Plus the dipping sauce was - what else - more cheese. Yay. My red beans and rice was super yummo. I would consider their recipe more of a meat heavy chili-like variety, so I was super full after about 3/4 of the dish. It also came with an unexpected side of nicely toasted and buttered bread (probably from a po-boy loaf of something). Hints: you can walk upstairs to order food without having to go through the bar downstairs. There is a nice dog named Leroy who belongs to the bar area, make sure not to step on him/put your bar stool on his tail!

text: Dined here on a Friday evening over the Labor Day holiday. We made reservations via Opentable which was key, as the place was packed and we never saw a vacant table. The main dining area is attached to a relatively open kitchen. The dining area has extremely high ceilings and is dimly lit. The tables are somewhat close together, however you don't feel like you are sitting on top of each other. It's a good date spot. The boyfriend and I each decided to do the $39 per person tasting menu. Before getting to the food, I must mention the drink each of us got and enjoyed immensely. The "Smoke on the Water" was absolutely fabulous. Complementing the liquor was a devilish combination of pepper and lime. This drink is smooth (and potentially dangerous). Luckily, I was able to keep it to two during dinner. Before the mezes arrived, the salatim and hummus arrived at the table with a seasoned laffa. The beets, the carrots, and the eggplant were standouts for me. The hummus was probably the best I've ever had. The mezes were all wonderful. The fried cauliflower was so unique as these golden nuggets sat in the bowl, you wondered what type of fried taste it would have. It's a surprisingly light dish. Another standout was the watermelon and feta salad. I also loved the chicken liver mousse on challah bread which had been lightly grilled. For the main course, I had the duck kebabs. I've never seen it on a menu and was excited to try it. It did not disappoint. The ground duck was perfectly grilled as kebabs and came with rice. After the main course, we were both nearing max capacity, but definitely wanted to sample some dessert. We each got a dessert. The stone fruit came with a nectarine sorbet was a great palate cleanser. We also got the chocolate almond cigars with chocolate mousse. It was hard to go wrong with either of those. Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience. Two small knocks on the place. 1. It was absolutely freezing at our table - bring a sweater just in case. 2. The background music was a tad too loud.

text: I had one of the top three best meals of my life last night at Sidney Street Cafe, and I don't even know how I'm going to write a review that comes close to doing it justice. If you haven't been here yet, clear the calendar and get yourself over there as soon as you can. I mean, President Obama DID choose Sidney Street for his meal on Tuesday night while he was in town... The Cardinals were playing last night so we sat at the bar instead of the dining room (which is beautiful by the way) and I'm actually really glad we did. Peggy, the bartender/server/wealth of knowledge, took great care of us and it was fun to interact with her, the staff, and the other bar go-ers throughout the meal. We had a great bottle of wine but I did notice they have an excellent by-the-glass menu if you aren't in the mood for an entire bottle. They can also make any cocktail your heart desires! We were pleasantly surprised when the chef sent out something new on the house for us to try, and he called it their take on breakfast. It was layered with snow peas on the bottom, whipped eggs, cheese, and slices of ham on top -- so good! I was scared of the whipped eggs (I'm a texture freak) but he assured me they were fully cooked before whipped. After the wine arrived we knew it was time to make appetizer decisions, so we ended up getting the sampler which is hands down the best way to go. It comes with: -Veal Dumplings: These things melt in your mouth and are tangy and so satisfying. -Honey Mustard Shrimp: This was wrapped in bacon and I'm not a huge fan of shrimp but I loved the flavor. -Lobster Turnovers: Best thing on the plate, for sure. You might want to order an extra. -Jumbo Lump Crab Cake: Also delicious, and didn't have that fishy taste that usually keeps me from eating them. The sampler comes with one of each item, so if you're with someone else make sure you each get your own. If someone tried to take a bite of that lobster turnover with me I'd probably stab them with my fork! Make sure you save room for an entree... I ended up getting the "local pork offering" which last night was a slow roasted shoulder, served over a blend of tomatoes, eggplant, and spices. This is where my words can't do this place justice -- I can't even begin to describe how incredible this dish was. It was served with corn hush puppies and a red pepper cream sauce. I think they should put this one permanently on the menu. This isn't somewhere to go all the time because it's pretty pricey, but save it for special occasions, birthdays, dates, etc... or if you're like me, save it to see the Cards win the NLDS. Couldn't have picked a better spot to spend the evening!

text: Delicious, but 5-star ratings are reserved for the best of the best. Staff: Friendly, attentive, fairly prompt. Ambience / Decor: Small dining room adjoining a small bar. Walls primarily black, strong bright red and turmeric-orange accents with wide strips of chromed diamond plate sheetmetal around the crown of the walls. Food: Good - quite enjoyable, but not top-shelf My Experience: I walked in with my 1 & 1/2-year-old at 7 PM on a Saturday, with downtown being fairly active (roller derby just 1 block away, and lots of foot traffic in the area). I was seated immediately and given my preference of table (a big plus with the kiddo along for the ride). The place was not perticularly busy, maybe 1/3rd of the tables were occupied. Within 3 minutes my drink order had been taken, and before 10 minutes had gone by I had my dinner order in. I ordered the 1/2-rack of St. Louis style BBQ ribs, and had French Fries & house salad (instead of the corn bread, as another Yelper had a pretty choice opinion on how bad the corn bread was). My food was up in about 15min (no surprise, since ribs are always pre-cooked and generally only need to be cut and sauced if they are ordered 'wet'.). The ribs were good, but aren't going to win any prizes. My guess is they use their own dry-rub & smoking technique but sadly they defer to a local Nevada company for the sauce which to me is a bit of a no-no when your establishment's signature IS BBQ. Anyhow, as I said the ribs were good, extremely fall-off-the-bone-tender and well-seasoned with a great char/sear on the outside. The french fries looked like they were cut in-house, and were perfectly crispy. The house salad was a nice fresh spring mix with toasted, candied pecans and what I believe was a blueberry-balsamic vinaigrette (a strange choice for a house salad at a BBQ joint, in my opinion). The vinaigrette was pretty powerful but the toasted, candied pecans really balanced out the acidity extremely well (I made sure each bite had some of the pecan once I figured that out). All in all, the experience was pleasant. My only knock might have been that the staff were a tiny bit slower than I might have desired, but it would be nitpicking if I let that color my review at all. I'd say 4 stars well-earned, these guys are a cut above Chili's, reasonably priced, with good flavors to their dishes.

(Though I will always have a soft spot in my heart for Vientiane on Baltimore Avenue.) The dumplings were delicate and addictively delicious, and I desperately wanted to keep eating the pad thai noodles until there was nothing left on the plate. Total bill, $39 for two people, including Thai iced tea. Unfortunately, we sensed they really didn't want any post-closing lingerers, so we got the rest of our meal to take out, which I ate guiltily in front of the TV around midnight. Just as we finished, our piping hot Thai pizza arrived, also 12-inch and more than enough for two. Baked perfectly, this delicious pie was popping with chicken, zuke, tomatoes, onion, and pine nuts (we added those for $1). The ambience here is sweet and romantic, despite Renee's obvious popularity. We never felt rushed even though I know folks were waiting for tables. The service is swift, polite, and thoughtful. . This will be an ongoing update as I work my way through the menu; the salads and melts sound decadent. I plan to try the "Steve and Isabel" mosh that Corey suggested as soon possible. text: I want to love PYT. The burgers have been delicious on each of my four visits. However, the service is so awful, so aloof, so slow, that I just can't give more stars. My first two visits were on the slower side but nothing extraordinary or worth a complaint online. Then I returned for a third time. After raving about the burgers, my boyfriend and I went for lunch on a week day. We were one of perhaps 5 or 6 tables, around 12:30 pm. He ordered some variety of veggie burger, I had a chicken burger. We didn't see our waitress again for nearly half an hour. It then took another 15 minutes to return with drink refills. Another good 15-20 minutes later the food arrived. Now everything was on point, or so I thought. Instead we waited until our food was nearly cold to receive a bottle of ketchup, and then sat with our dirty dishes for another 15 waiting on the check. Look, I get it, it's a hipster stop, blah blah blah. But they have a pretty solid product to put out there, why screw it up with subpar service? As a former waitress, I know it can be rough faking interest and attentiveness when you'd rather be home sleeping off a hangover or cracking the books for class and instead you're working long tough hours on your feet and you go home every night smelling like grease. But with so many people who wish they had jobs in the country, I'd like a little more effort from a server. Like it or not, you're working in an industry where your costumers have a direct impact on your ability to pay your bills. Wait, let me redact that rant. I forgot, PYT feels the need to include my gratuity for me. I like to consider myself a pretty generous tipper. I also like to think that this country was built on a principle of self-autonomy. I don't appreciate a restaurant forcing my hand to tip 18%. If 20-25% is industry standard for basic decent service, I feel like 18% is overtipping at PYT.

text: This was a not a great experience for my family and me. The restaurant was really hot and there was no air movement. The place was fairly crowed so I figured the burgers must be really good if everyone was there eating in such an uncomfortable environment. Like the reviewer below I figured it had to be at least in the mid 80's in there. Hot enough that after sitting there for a little bit my forehead had sweat running down it, my shirt was starting to get wet, and my wife and I were getting concerned for our 8 month old son. When we were placing our order I asked the girl at the register if the air condition was broken. I thought sure I was asking a question that had an obvious answer. However she sad "no, it's always this hot in here". Looking back I should have walked out right then and there. Beside the fact that it was uncomfortable I don't see how it could be good to have an open toppings bar sitting in those temperatures. The next issue was the floor. There was a coating of grease that made the floor extremely slippery. There was one yellow slippery floor sign up by the toppings bar where the grease was very heavy. Heavy enough that you could see shoe marks in it. The grease made it as slippery as ice and I found it easier to just slide my feet than actually walk. This place is a lawsuit waiting to happen! After we left my wife told me that while we were ordering she saw one of the employees bring back an order of fries from a table. She told the cook they were supposed to be seasons and not plain. The cook then dumped them right back into the fries bin rather than putting them in the trash. I'm pretty sure places aren't supposed to serve food that has already been sent out to another table. I really can't give a fair review of the food. I was so uncomfortable and I was eating so fast that I don't even really remember the burger. Plus it was sort of gross to have my feet sliding around under the table as I ate. It blew my mind when I found out this place was a chain. I thought sure some dude that has no clue how to run a restaurant opened this place up and was trying to make a go of it. I would be surprised if this place makes it through the end of the year. text: I went to this place recently with my wife because I had a restaurant.com gift certificate for some time I needed to use up. But, that doesn't change the taste test and the moderate inflexibility with the create your own dish option. the spring rolls were good, as far as spring rolls can be.... veggie pot stickers only had cabbage in it and was very bland.... kimchi was forgettable (and i'll just leave at that).... chow fun I - i thought was ok. but my wife hated it. there were lumps of noodles stuck together with minimal sauce on them - making the dish less than appetizing. But, there were lots and lots of bean sprouts in the dish - as promised by the waiter. Massaman thai curry - this was the first time trying this dish. So, I didn't know what to expect. The veggies were in HUGE chunks & half cooked. The tofu was really good. Even though there was no spiciness to the dish, it was the only palatable item on our table. So, we enjoyed it. Get this, they DON'T have a desert menu........ I'd say, if I didn't have the restaurant.com GC, I wouldn't pick or recommend this place. text: Wait... I've NEVER reviewed Sun King? How is this possible? I'm with friend Rachael W... I must have just been putting it off unconsciously. Anyway, Sun King is what I would consider the birth of the craft beer movement in Central Indiana. I know Upland was all up on that before Sun King came into the picture, but Sun King's presence in the city has been magnificently marketed and brilliantly executed. Everywhere you want local beer, you can find Sun King, if you can find any. All of their beers... ALL of them, even the ones I don't prefer the style of, are great. When I go for a tasting or growler fill--which doesn't happen as often as I'd like nowadays--I always try everything, and I've never found one to disappoint. Even the Walking On The Sun chile-infused beer. Lately, I fell in love with the Indiana Landmarks Wit, which is one of my favorite beers in a long time. Their website is well done, allowing easy exposure and education to their beers. The tasting room... and I remember way back when there were no taps, no AC, just tables and pitchers and people lovin' beer, has developed into a streamlined, energizing place where everyone from IUPUI Coeds to My Parent's Aged beer oficionados (no offense!) can be found on a Friday sippin' 3oz cups and doing Friday $5 fills. Basically, if you want to learn about beer, go to Sun King. If you want to get introduced to the craft beer scene, go to Sun King. If you want to start sampling the local beers in Indianapolis, go to Sun King. Then go to the other great breweries including Fountain Square, Flat 12, Triton and Upland. Also, Black Acre if they're open (not sure.) (shameless plugs abouding!).

text: This review is for the buffet only. After going through pages of the reviews on Yelp, I was extremely excited to try this place even though I live in the opposite side of the city. But I was kind of disappointed with the lack of vegetable dishes - you'll probably get more selection on the salad/cold dishes side. I personally love chicken but oh my goodness, that's a little overkilled. And finally for the dessert, I should've trust my instinct and go with the mango ice cream. But since I've seen people raving the "milkballs" I was totally ready to give them a try. BAD DECISION! The very first bite I took taste like diabetes exploded in my mouth...no kidding. It was overwhelmingly sweet with the mushy texture that kind of gross me out. Regarding to the flavor, there's nothing special about it - if anyone's familiar with the taste of condensed milk, that's pretty much what the milk balls taste like except they've been drenched in honey which making them 10000x sweeter than they already are. The whole time I just think about mango ice cream. *sigh* Overall, this place wasn't bad - certainly not the best I've been to for Indian food. I think I'll walk the extra 10 steps to get my Indian food fix at Tandoor next time. :)

text: We got the Travelzoo deal - $99 for five course dinner at Bella Vista at The Four Seasons hotel! I was expecting really high class, fine dining, since this is the four seasons, after all. But surprisingly, it was not really super stuffy or high class. Food was good and definitely high class, but not the best meal I've ever had. Decor: very cute. High ceilings and a beautiful view of the ocean from the inside. We went on a weekend where it was cloudy and possible rainy so they didn't open up the outside patio for dinner guests. Decor reminded me a lot like I was on vacation on a tropical island. Bright yellow and blue color table settings and flowers. Straw-like-looking chairs. Drapings hung from the ceiling. They gave us a complimentary bread basket. I loved the tomato sauce that came with it! Sweet and lots of tomato paste flavor! I forgot the brown-colored bread but it was pretty good. I also like the thin bread that taste like parmesan cheese crisps. I didn't taste the sourdough because I wanted to save room for the food. First course: Wild mushroom burrata cheese grilled bruschetta - Pretty good! Burrata cheese was really creamy. Put lots of pepper on it. It also came with arugula mixed with olive oil. Eat the arugula with the bruschetta and cheese to get nice contrasting flavors and texture. The arugula by itself is a little too bitter (even though I love arugula). Second course: Tagliatelle pasta with braised short ribs, pickled lemon and Bloomsdale spinach. - I LOVE braised short ribs. This dish was good but I think this dish has been pretty common with all the other travelzoo/groupon/livingsocial/opentable deals we've had. I kinda felt it wasn't super unique anymore. Flavor was good. YOu could definitely taste the lemon! Short ribs were ok. My fiancee loved this dish. Third course: Local halibut with fennel puree and taggiasca black olives. - My fiancee was disappointed that he only got one olive. Me, too! The fish was cooked well and had a nice crispy exterior. But I agree with my fiancee. It was kinda bland. Perhaps it was placed in this order to cleanse our palate. The fennel puree and fennel was yummy. Fourth course: Sonoma lamb chop with minted artichokes, sun-dried tomato, goat cheese and green farro. - Our waitress recommended getting it medium rare. I don't like raw meat. So I got mine medium. And I normally don't like lamb. But this was delicious!!! Probably my 2nd favorite of the five course meal. The lamb was cooked and didn't have a game-y after taste. The goat cheese with the sun-dried tomato flavor farro really complimented the lamb really well! It was delicious! Fifth course: Passion fruit panna cotta with pistachio and blood orange sorbet. - This was DELICIOUS!! Oh my goodness...plenty of panna cotta. The tartness of the passion fruit panna cotta was deliciously paired with the crunchiness of the pistachio and the sweet/tart blood orange sauce, as well as the crunchy nut mixture and cool blood orange sorbet. YUM, YUM! My favorite dish of the night. Even though I was so full from eating all day, I licked off every last bite. Service: Pretty good. They filled our water glasses and brought each plate. Hostess was also nice and friendly. The Four Seasons is pretty nice hotel, too. I liked their bathrooms!! Overall, thank you to Travelzoo for the deal! We had a great dinner. Yum.

text: I remember the days growing up in an Eastern Time zone when going to Red Lobster was kind of a big deal. It was a Fri or Sat night affair, you had some nice duds on and a bit of cash to burn. The standards of both Red Lobster and Olive Garden (see my previous reviews on that) have slipped considerably. And when I am paying $30 a plate plus drinks, I still want good service, great food and a nice feeling when I am leaving knowing that I am appreciated! We had a long day in Edmonton, driving there and back same day from Calgary. I was craving seafood so - where else to go but Red Lobster? Entryway, the door was filthy. Ew, grimy. OK, inside will be better... Nope, no way Jose. inside, carpets were sooo filthy and littered and it was only 3pm! What kind of a crazy lunch service did they have? Not to have drink coasters thrown at me by the baby 1 metre from our table. And there were Cheerios all underneath our table... OK, so I thought I better have a drink. Vodka/cranberry. Poor thing, the drink came back with the saddest ice, almost all melted into my drink by the time it arrived at the table. Ordered entrees, clam chowder to start. Lukewarm. The flavour was there but am I strange to like my soup hot? Almost an HOUR went by as we waited for our entree. It is not like we got an app with the meal, just our included soup. I noted my seafood (lobster and shrimp) upon trying it was is blaringly rare and inedible. I had already seen one lady send her lobster back for it being raw. And I DO like rare things. But not my seafood. I advised the waitress I would take my food home and heat it up properly myself as it was just not cooked. She advised that "the chef thought how he cooked it was fine"... Hmmm not so, I cook lobster all the time and it is not supposed to be near runny! She offered to bring another out - I asked for a box to take it to go. I proceeded to the washroom and on the way passed a female manager who was eating a meal. I would have preferred her over at my table apologizing for her chef. The soap dispenser hanging off the wall by barely 1 screw was charming. I was shaking my head wondering what had happened to this restaurant chain. For 2 days, honestly I have not been feeling the best from that meal. I called the GM as his # was on the bottom of the receipt for any comments or questions! Hell ya! I called and got the run around that he was in, oh no he was not in and they were not sure when he was in next. When they went to check his schedule, the staff never came back onto the phone leaving me to stew even more! Hey, he had a chance to explain himself before I posted this review! This will be one restaurant that I will miss in a way but it is time to simply Bless and Release this one... I do not think they could ever recover at this point, it is too far gone and Management does not seem to care. Sad, I had some good memories at Red Lobster.. 20 years ago.

text: My friend and I took the Original Creole New Orleans tour. It was a low key 3ish hour tour of the Bywater, on comfortable, well-padded bicycles. They provided helmets and cold water, and every bicycle had a basket in which to store your possessions. Our tour guide was Cassidy, and he was amazing. This tour is fun, funny, and provides a very interesting and personal history of the city. Cassidy was knowledgeable and had a clear affection for New Orleans. The tour consisted of both the historical origins of many of New Orleans' cultural tradition, as well as a unique insight to more modern events and the unique personality of this city. I would honestly recommend this tour very strongly. Though I was enjoying my trip before the tour, I found that after the tour I had a better understanding of and appreciation for the city and its quirks. Do not take this tour expecting measured stops and dry descriptions of architecture and important historical events. Do take it expecting funny voices, bad accents, stories of french aristocrats in dresses, and ultimately a sense of fondness for the city's idiosyncrasies. Also of note is that our tour guide spent a solid half hour answering questions about good places to find specific kinds of food and entertainment, and gave us all his cell phone number so that we could text him if we got lost or needed guidance. They were all very kind and generous with their time and advice, and it was really cool to see first-hand how strong the sense of community is in the city--so many people recognized and had a brief word with our guide as we rode by.

Never in my life have I ordered a veggie omelet to have it come out like this, usually it has tomatoes, bell peppers, onion, mushrooms, etc. I couldn't even believe it. Oh and it had a slice of yucky government like american cheese on the top. The egg portion of the omelet was crispy on the edges and rubbery, beyond anything I would ever want to eat. the "toast" (I use that term loosely) had the most miraculous thing going on that I have ever seen in my life. it was warmed bread in the middle (not toasted at all) and burnt black edges. It really defied the laws of science. I should have saved it for prosperity as i doubt I will ever see anything like it again. Oh and the bread since it was just bread in the middle had no butter, it was as if it was too much work for the "chef" to actually butter the toast, and tasted like the plastic bag I am certain it was housed in. The grits were pasty and cold, the hashbrowns were overwhelmed with Tony's seasoning and it seemed clear they were not fresh made. They tasted like they were cooked a few hours before we arrived, re heated and cooled off. A blend of salty over seasoned, cold greasy burnt-ness. Like I said basically the only decent thing was the coffee. The service was terrible and the waitstaff seemed very inconvenienced by the few people that were in there. We asked them what was included in some items and they had to run into the kitchen to find out. On top of that my friend asked for sauteed mushrooms (again she had to check with the kitchen) the waitress told us they had it but when the plate came she said "oh we ran out." Yeah I think it was more like she forgot to put it on the order and didn't want to go back and fix it. I was a bit mad at myself because I have seen enough episodes of Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares to know that this place had all the red flags! I totally ignored all of them. Funny thing is they have comment cards (which I actually filled out) but I doubt that they will take the comments seriously. If they want comments, they should read Yelp! Needless to say I won't be back, and don't recommend that you waste your time going there. Head to Russell's and just endure the wait to get a good meal.
