text: Went to Chappy's this week on business. My co-workers had really hyped this place so I was pretty psyched. I've spent a lot of time in New Orleans so was really excited about authenitc cajun cuisine. The ambiance was pretty blah. Nothing too exciting, Walls were very plain. Would have expected more NOLA themes around the place. We were there at 6 and the place was fairly empty. Even then, service was generally slow. The menu is generous, with most entree's in the $20-25 range. For appetizers, we ordered crab cakes, blackened shrimp and tuna tar tare for the table of 6. The crab cakes were very good (and that's saying a lot for a Maryland native!). They weren't Maryland style lump, but they were tasty, seasoned well and cooked perfectly. The shrimp overcooked and salty, which was truly foreshadowning of the rest of the meal. Even the tuna had a very salty rub on the exterior. For my entree, I ordered the blackened redfish, which was recommended by one of my co-workers. As described int he menu: "marinated in butter, sprinkled with Chappy's spices, pan fried to perfection and served with maMAma's shrimp and eggplant." I asked if the fish could be just grilled, without the butter, but the server recommended against it. Though the fish itself was cooked perfectly, nice and flaky, I'd swear there was a pound of salt in the rub. The shrimp and eggplant side was the highlight of the dinner -- very tasty. This was a company meal with locals that loved the place, so I didn't complain, but this wasn't close to the meals I've had in the French Quarter or, in most other cajun places in other place. You know how sometimes you have a meal that you're disappointed with but chalk it up to a bad night so you'll try it again? Well, this isn't one of them. I'm sure there are better places in Music City next time I'm there.

text: I have been a resident of South Jersey for a little over two years now. I guess I wasn't around during the Mansion's heyday. Whenever I mention the Mansion people say "Oh its not at good as it used to be". When we moved to Voorhees 2 years ago, we were on a quest to find a great place for Sunday brunch. After reading a few reviews, we decided to try the Mansion a couple of months after moving to South Jersey. At that price we were not impressed. The food seemed bland, and it looked as if someone allowed a kindergarten class create the menu with drawings. This past Sunday we went back to the Mansion for the Peach Festival Sunday brunch. I guess word is spreading that the Mansion was falling off because we were pleased with brunch today. I could be wrong, but I felt like there were more options to choose from. Were there a few issues? Yes, the coffee was not very good. There was no cream on the table so my cup sat there until I was able to get my waiter to bring some over. Upon arriving there is only one host that greets and seats everyone so it took a little time be seated. Please forgive me if this a religions thing but cheese blintzes and french toast do not belong in the same chaffing dish. One of my main concerns was regarding the bill. A 21% gratuity was applied to each individual in the party; there were only two of us. This was my second visit in two years and I can't remember if a gratuity charge was applied to the bill on my first visit. I was a little taken by the fact that gratuity was applied to a party of only two. I always tip above 18% and that's usually off the total check so I am not a fan of establishments adding gratuity, I feel it only hurts the servers. I added something extra but couldn't help but feel as if I didn't leave enough. After we got down the road, my wife asked if the 21% was for the buffet workers. I figured thats what it probably was, then I felt even worse. Instead of listing it as a gratuity the Mansion should list it as a service charge. I worked in the food industry and have eaten at plenty of buffets and I am not familiar with that process. The Sunday brunch at the Mansion is not going to make my top 10 list, but it's not Coast Line. Between the places in Northern Liberties and my favorite restaurant for brunch, K.C. Prime Steakhouse in Mercer County I probably won't be here again until the next Peach Festival.

text: I know that everyone seems to love this place, but after trying this place many times, on and off, over the past few years we remain underwhelmed. Upfront I have to say that we've never tried Datz for dinner, just for breakfast and lunch. Their lunch is OK in terms of the food, their sandwiches overall are tasty - and big! - and the homemade chips always please. However, I don't recommend the breakfast or brunch. We live in the neighborhood and sometimes go there for breakfast when we want to stay close to home or when other places are closed, and we're always disappointed. We've had soggy eggs, pancakes that were raw in the middle, and one time we got served a bagel that had mold on it (this was maybe two years ago and the manager on duty came out and apologized profusely to us, but we didn't go back there for at least 6 months after that incident). We ate breakfast there again today and I ordered simple scrambled eggs with toast and turkey bacon. The eggs were blah and the turkey bacon wasn't very good. It was really limpy and thin - not crisp at all. The service at Datz always ranges from mediocre to poor, and today it was on the poor side for sure. It took the server 5-10 minutes to come over to our table for the first time just to get us water. I ordered coffee and apparently they were out of coffee and brewing some more (how can a good restaurant be low on coffee during breakfast service??). It took another 5-10 minutes before she finally brought be a cup. I noticed that other tables got a small carafe of coffee served at their table, but I got just one cup. Before the food arrived, a customer who was leaving walked by our table and spilled his to-go cup of coffee all over the table, the floor and on me. There was a server (not ours) standing right next to us, but instead of rushing to help us she ran the other way. In fact, nobody came over for several minutes, so we started to mop up the spilled coffee ourselves with our napkins. Finally, a different person (not our server, who had disappeared, or the one who ran away) came over to help, but by that time we had gotten up most of the spilled coffee ourselves. She asked if we wanted new napkins (well, the two we had were soaked with coffee that we had mopped up, so that was a really dumb question). Our server never did come over to help. The food also took an usually long time to arrive. We definitely won't be back to Datz for breakfast ever again. We may try them again for lunch in a pinch, but that's about it.

text: Summary: Great food, big portions, kind of expensive! Remember when all your friends were turning 21 one-by-one? Remember all those crazed nights, with the sheer awesomeness of complete randomness? Yeah. This was one of those nights. (Gosh... now I feel old) Anyways... I'd gone here with 2 of my friends, one of whom was turning the glorious two-one. We had drinks (both variants - some boozed up and some sans-alcohol) flowing all through the night, appetizers, entrees, and dessert. Aka, we didn't skimp out on anything. We went for the real deal. (Disclaimer: For the safety and security of your wallet and credit line, I recommend that you avoid doing this.) Libations consisted of several different margaritas (El Vez, Pink Cadillac, and Golden), some specialties (Julep and Sangria Blanca), and the Michelada. They make great variants of most of them in the virgin and alcoholic variants, and I personally can attest for the awesomeness of the Sangria Blanca and the Michelada. The Sangria was absolutely spot on - correct sweetness, correct flavoring - and it hit the spot. Appetizers were the traditional El Vez guacamole (awesome as usual - get it), the Mexican Chopped Salad, and the Queso Fundido De Hongos. I wasn't particularly fond of the latter two, but as I mentioned, go for the guacamole. You won't be sad. Then again, the Queso was a hit at my table, but just not with me, so take my recommendation with a grain of salt (or cheese?). Mains consisted of the pollo annatto, the huarache de hongos (vegetarian), and the pasilla braised pork. I can't speak for the non-veg dishes, but the huarache was absolutely phenomenal. The sauces were spicy and delectable, the veggies were cooked perfectly, and they were awesome. The other guys really liked their mains too, so I'd venture to guess that all 3 are pretty good. Dessert was just churros and flan. Oh wait. I can't say 'just.' It was AWESOME churros and flan. Really really good stuff. Mouth-gasm inducing stuff. Yeah. That good. Other friends who've visited haven't raved as much about the desserts, so maybe it was just good luck on a good night, but they were fantastic. Service was great as well, and our server was very helpful and attentive to our table, even though the place was packed and she had a ton of other tables to work with. The one downside? 65$ per person (78$ including tip) at the end of the night. Granted, we had a ton of food and drinks, it was a great evening, and going in, we knew that our wallets would be lighter at the end of the evening, but some of the items are still overpriced. However, if money is no concern - go here. It'll be a fun visit. If it is a concern... well. Save up! :)

text: This review is for the Jazz Brunch. I've been twice. Both times were amazing. I am sad that so many people give this restaurant bad reviews. Let's clarify a few things: It's a brunch BUFFET. That being said, the history is so thick in there, you can see it. The employees are the most knowledgeable and helpful individuals on the planet. The jazz music and tablescapes are nice, the courtyard is absolutely amazing. The food- well, it may not be the most "gourmet", no one is paying attention to your individual plate. However, it is delicious. It is not only delicious, it's yummy enough for me to go back again and again and again. The creamed spinach is to die for. And their omelette/eggs benedict station is a treat. My mouth is watering just thinking about it. Advice: If you're visiting NO, this is a quintessential place to go for brunch. Go early. Make a reservation. It's clean and delicious. I do not love buffets, they usually gross me out. This place is an exception. If you have to go late, or don't like the idea of food being picked over, or the idea that your food is prepared for the masses- go somewhere else.

text: I want to preface this review by saying that I went during restaurant week. With that said, I've had amazing meals at some very high end restaurants during previous restaurant weeks and to say that I was extremely let down at La Famiglia is an understatement. We were greeted warmly by the hostess who seated our party of 6. Within minutes, the waiter came back with restaurant week menus that were tattered and stained. While we were deciding on food, he brought out a basket of bread that was incredibly stale. I only ate a couple of pieces because I was starving. Ok, not off to a good start so far. I ended up ordering the sea scallop salad, anticipating 2-3 large sea scallops on a bed of lettuce and veggies. When it came to the table, I was disappointed. Instead of finding large, meaty sea scallops, I was given mixed greens with tiny sea scallop turds. They tasted like they were either frozen or straight out of can. Actually, I could barely taste them because they were so miniscule. There was nothing else on the salad, which bored my taste buds. Bleh. Since I'm lactose intolerant, most of the pasta dishes were out of the question for the main course, so I ordered a medium rare steak and veggies. You can't screw that up, right? Not only was I unimpressed with my first course, but I was also disappointed with the service. My table waited over 30 minutes to get our second course! When my meal finally came out, I really had to contain my disappointment as to appear polite in front of our dinner guests. Not only was my steak and the sauce covering it mediocre, it was definitely cooked over medium rare and had very little seasoning. The steak was served with a small portion of mashed potatoes and veggies, which were definitely frozen, microwaved, and dumped on a plate. Seriously? Hoping the restaurant could redeem themselves with dessert, I waited in anticipation. We were all served 3 small cakes (chocolate, ricotta cheese, and some orange cake) that were again very mediocre. If this is supposed to be fine dining, then Olive Garden is leaps and bounds ahead of this restaurant. Get it together La Famiglia. I will definitely never be back. Thank god the entire meal only cost $35 because I have no idea how people fork over hundreds of dollars to dine here.

I don't know if it's made in-house or they buy it from a vendor, but the slaw is the perfect side for the chicken; cool and creamy, with a hint of pepper. Like french fries? The ones at Speck's are crinkle cut and fried to perfection. Get a meal, and you'll get a little dinner roll, with a pat of butter, and a wet-nap. Oh, and for the ultimate experience, be sure to get a packet of honey and drizzle the honey on your chicken. SO GOOD! I think Speck's has burgers, and other items, but even though I've been eating here for decades, I always get the chicken. You should too.

text: Oh wow wow, what a night, what a menu, what a fabulous experience at Cibo! I made a fairly last minute reservation, a few days ahead, but for a group of 10. We arrived and were placed in a long table that is on a riser that looks down on the rest of the tiny bistro. The wine and champagne were flowing, the conversation a flutter and I was surrounded by so many good friends, there was no way this was going to be a bad meal. And, it lived up to the hype! CIbo, like Lea mentions, is pronounced Chee-bo and sounds super fancy but in Italian it just means food! Haha, could you imagine walking the streets of Rome and seeing a place called Food? Speaking of food, lets get to it! I like to try a lot of different things, and Cibo is a great place to go with a group and do shared plates. We had the Zeppole, which usually I love, but I found a bit bland, however, that was the low point (and it was still quite good, just not mind blowing like I know the tiny donuts can be). Every other item we ordered was phenomanal! I loved the Charcuterie Board, it is now in my YEG top 5 boards. The trio of bruschetta was so so good, all three types were delicious and way beyond most average bruschettas, my favorite of the three was definatly the prosciutto di parma topped with quail egg. I could eat those all day long! The Cheese board was fabulous, but it's hard to screw up cheese. The pan fried ricotta cakes were wonderful, and had a delightful tomato basil jam on the side. And finally, we had the polpette, they were big juicy flavor packed veal and pork meatballs that were to die for! Cibo is definatly a fabulous restaurant, I highly recomend it if you are looking for somewhere special for a small group!

We also tried the lamb carpaccio, which came out in a huge, incredibly tasty mound so big we couldn't finish it between the two of us, despite our best efforts. It had the texture of prosciutto, tender and soft, and I wish I had it in me to eat more of it than I did! For pasta we had the the fettucini with a meat sauce which I sadly cannot remember any more detail about, but it was incredibly tasty and was quickly devoured. We paired that with the I-knew-I-was-getting-it-the-second-I-saw-it-on-the-menu tortelloni stuffed with veal sweetbreads in a brown butter sauce. My god. I remain immensely sad that only two of those four, plump, perfect fried (I think!) sweetbread dumplings were mine. Incredibly tasty. The service at Popolino was every bit as good as at Modo Mio, and that's saying something. I don't know how McAndrews explains the tone of service to his staff, but there are some other spots in town that could stand to borrow it. Being there was a delight. Popolino is cash only, and BYOB.

I wasn't dumbfounded, I was lost in my own thoughts again... could i genetically engineer a child to have a fast metabolism so it could join me on my culinary adventures without being obese? Clearly these adventures are no place for children. "If you and I did this, it would definitely need my nose and my boobs." Really? You are a man, you don't have boobs. Oh shit neither do I. Our one issue was with the brussels sprouts salad--perhaps it was a difference of expectations. The sprouts came less cooked that we'd expected, and the stilton seemed weak and something of an afterthought (see the above reverie about cheese). Main courses were seared hanger steak with pomme frites (fantastic) and duck cassoulet (also fantastic). Dessert, however, was my favorite--the raspberry chambord cake, amazingly light and flavorful. I thought I'd be too full for dessert--kids, I was not. Get that cake. Other perks: waiter was attentive but not overly so; there is a tree growing in the middle of the dining room and out the top of the restaurant. Full sized trees indoors make me smile.

text: Only because my favorite Deli (Rachel's Nosherai) is now closed on Sunday due to a death in the family, and because my favorite cousins suggested it, we four had brunch today at the 19th street branch of the 4th Street Famous Deli. This is the perfect number of people to share a meal at the Famous, since its owner is busy charging exorbitant prices for enormous portions of mediocre food, that are edible only by a family of four. When we entered this establishment, we saw a bemused couple seated in front of a mound of corn beef hash the size of a small infant, about twelve inches long and four inches high.. We commented to them that it was enough to feed a family of four but they disagreed and showed us that it was more than enough for a family of eight. My wife and I agreed to share a single smoked fish sandwich, by ordering an extra portion of pumpernickle. I ordered my favorite, jumbo whitefish on rye with cream cheese tomato and onion. My cousin remarked, only half in jest" Remember to ask them to remove the tail". What came to the table was a fresh four inch slice of jumbo white fish, freshly cut of the fish both sides, untouched by human hands. Having worked in a number of Delis I proceeded to filet the fish myself , carefully cutting along the backbone inside and then removing the spine and ribs on one side and picking out the spineless ribs on the other and then pulling the skin away from the two fresh moist filets. The rye and pumpernickel was sliced much too thick for our tastes. About a half inch thick. I then smeared the cream cheese on the bread, added the fish and the tomato and onion, sliced the two sandwiches in half and presented one on my wife's plate. The resulting sandwiches I had created were delightful, made from wholesome ingredients. But I wondered why I was paying the Deli for making my own sandwiches.
label: NEG

The kitchen was very accommodating to me and allowed me to go with scrambled egg whites vs. poached eggs which I really appreciated. I went with the Eggs Florentine and the creamed spinach absolutely made the dish. The diced potatoes served on the side were mediocre and relatively unseasoned. A few of my girlfriends went with the famous Bloody Mary bar which looked like a blast. Should I return, that might be worth a shot. One thing to mention, they charge $3 for their fountain sodas (highway robbery). text: When my now-husband and I were planning our wedding, it seemed like we were on our own as far as accommodations post-reception. We initially felt like it would be O.K. for us to just....return back to our apartment, but when we saw a good deal for a room at the Sofitel on a discount travel website to which I subscribe, we went for it. Fast forward a few more weeks: we were gifted a hotel suite for our wedding night, and I transferred our Sofitel reservation to the weekend preceding my husband's birthday for only eleven dollars more (as opposed to other weekends about which I inquired, which cost upwards of $100 more to transfer the date). That being said, the staff, from my initial calls hoping that transferring prepaid reservation dates wouldn't be a hassle to every in-person interaction, was very friendly and accommodating without being cloying. The room is very nice but not a knockout as far as decor, although the French doors leading into the bathroom were an attractive touch. The bed, comforter, and pillows were remarkably comfortable, and I have a serious case of Princess and the Pea slash Goldilocks syndrome (too hard, too soft, too lumpy, too firm, too hot, too cold, too many pillows, pillows too flat, fidget, flip over, curl up, splay out, etc., etc). The bathroom was spacious and clean--my favorite part of our room. The bathroom featured lemony L'Occitane bath goods (my husband noted that the lotion smelled like Pez). The room service menu appeared extensive and actually appealing in its selection of items both comfort food-y (cheesesteaks, pizza, popcorn), luxurious (cheese plate options abound), and fresh and light (hummus platter, seafood timbales with avocado and greens), although we did not partake. The gym facilities were pleasant, clean, and well-maintained. The weight machines were up-to-date and in excellent condition (more recent models than my neighborhood gym, no disrespect to my local). There were a number of treadmills, and two ellipticals and stationary bikes as well. The above-and-beyond touches in the fitness room included the complimentary water by the machines (YAY!), free red and green apples, and headphones with removable earpads for those wanting to use the TV screens attached to the 'mills. (I generally don't when I'm ordinarily at the gym, but I gave it a whirl in the hotel, and watched such quality programming as some sort of cartoon program composed of basically parody commercials, and an infomercial about an infared cooking apparatus). Later that night at the hotel bar, Liberte, my companion and I enjoyed beer, cocktails, and bub over hours of conversation so intense that we got choked up at various points. The atmosphere (fancy living-room-y with its large velvet chairs/couch/fireplace/dim lighting) is conducive to this type of chatting; this aspect of our experience was priceless, as the last couple of weeks have been spent doing the wake up beat/go to work/come home late/make dinner to eat listlessly/read the internet even more listlessly/go to bed daily grind, which is a heart, soul, and boner deflater. A con: neighboring patrons' loud TVs can be heard, as in the case of someone blasting a program at 5 am which seemed to consist entirely of two people yelling hysterically at each other, like porn for those who feel too repressed to emote. Noise from the street is also jarringly audible throughout the night; the dude letting out short, barking screams every couple of seconds until a female companion started shrieking alongside him managed to jar me out of sleep repeatedly. Unrelated but related, though: the elevators require you to use your key to access floors above the fourth. While minorly inconvenient, this is also nice in that it prevents situations like those I've experienced in other city hotels: random non-patrons partying in the hallway and awakening me or relatives from out of town in the wee hours of the morn. One other neg: the vestibule before entering the hotel lobby smelled faintly of garbage, which was off-putting, but this may not be a chronic issue. Of special note is the upfront and helpful concierge William, who managed to give us dinner recommendations that were a) super close to the hotel on a chilly night on which we wanted to neither walk/travel far nor pay for cab, b) satisfied my craving for hearty-but-healthy food, c) made my man and me moon over each other over the whole meal, d) subtly acknowledged/respected the fact that we're locals but wanted to try something cozy and different, and e) made us two Philadelphians feel like we were on a special intimate vacation even though we live about 15 minutes walking distance from the hotel, to the point that we kept forgetting, once we returned home, that we *hadn't* been in a different city on some brief whirlwind travel adventure.

text: We went to the Broad Axe Tavern on Friday night because we were looking to expand our local dining options. First off the decor was wonderful. They really did an excellent job renovating the interior. They successfully managed to keep the historical nature and style of the building while still giving it newer accouterments. Now onto the food. We started off with Wings and Fries as appetizers. The fries (Belgian Pommes Frites for the snooty amongst you) came with three dipping sauces, cheese, ketchup and ranch. (The sauces are fancier versions of those 3 but you get the idea) The fries were excellent, and the dipping sauces were all very good as well. The wings were a decent size and had good flavor. We went with mild because my mom was with us and wanted to have some so, I can't finish my normal wing breakdown commenting on the heat. For an entree I decided to try the Sauteed Tenderloin Tips with Chipotle Mashed Potatoes which was incredible. The tips were cooked absolutely perfectly and were loaded with flavor. The mashed potatoes were very good. I also tried a piece of my dad's Braised Short Ribs and they were very good as well. Fork tender and very flavorful. Our dinner experience was definitely 5 stars. In fact it was so good that when deciding where to go for brunch on Sunday morning we checked Broad Axe first to see if they served brunch. When we found they did we knew where we were heading. After how great dinner was brunch was a little bit of a let down. It wasn't bad necessarily, more just average. I had the Omelet and Sausage which were good enough, but nothing special. The best part of breakfast were the potatoes which were pretty good. That leaves me with a 5 for Dinner and an A-OK 3 for Brunch and a 4 star overall rating. We'll definitely be back for dinner in the future and will probably give the breakfast another shot too.
label: POS

text: I feel like an obstinate teenager writing this review. "Okay, FINE Mom. Aqui Con El Nene's Sonoran Hot Dogs were just as good if not maybe better then Guerro Canelo." I am something of a Sonoran Hot Dog connoisseur, and when someone told me these were better, I went along to humor them, knowing in the depths of my heart that they could not be better. Well, I will (reluctantly) admit that I was wrong. They were at least as good as Guerro, but I have to try them again to make the full judgement of if they were as good or if they were better. The bun, while also divine at Guerro, at Nene's was less doughy and....glutony? It was softer and more airy, though it could still definitely hold all of the fixins! Also, something that I judge very harshly at any place is the avocado sauce. I could drink the stuff most of the time. This one was absolutely better than Guerro. Don't get me wrong! Both are delicious! But the one here actually had a tiny little kick of heat to it, and as it turns out I super enjoyed it.

Everyone has a friend or a few who rave about some run of the mill Meximerican restaurant that is in there area of town..You have Los Palmas or Tres Amigos or whatever other generic name you can spit out. These places are pretty well interchangeable with menu items and thus should be rated on a different scale. You don't go to these places for farm fresh ingredients or a grass fed hanger steak tacos. You go for the food that you know what it tastes like before it gets to your table. So I have said that to give you my review of "My Mexican" restaurant. I have never been disapointed here, the service is excellent. The menu items are prepared quickly and come out hot and fresh. The salsa which is oh so important to many people is very good here, and this is an excellent spot to get an afterwork beer, especially the 34oz. Dos Equis. So basically what I am saying is...yes its a generic Mexican restaurant, and yes most things on the menu come covered in cheese with a side of beans, but if your ok with that, you will get good services, hot food, and at a very reasonable price.

This is filled with everything from beef, to seafood. Black beans and a wonderful white cheese filling is also included in many of the dishes, along with a sweet plantain, a small banana like fruit, which gives the most unique and delicious flavor I have ever tasted. text: Oh...a tiny breakfast. How quaint. After reading reviews extolling the virtues of Chhaya, I was anxious to witness this culinary righteousness for myself. My Lady and I agreed to blow off our usual brunch favourtites, and instead head over to E. Passyunk Street. We walked into a dining room which was slightly smaller than our living room, albeit tidy. We were immediately informed that there is no table service on the weekdays, lest we ask for more than we are entitled to. We sat down and perused le menu. Waffles seemed to be the speciality of the house, so we decided to try them. My CD sized waffle arrived at my table unaccompanied by any of the usual suspects...not even a lowly garnish. Lady Mary's breaky looked similarly lonely, but at least we each had a non-refillable $4 cup of coffee to keep our waffles company. The flavour wasn't at all bad, however. The sausage gravy was acceptably authentic (on mine), and nutella was used in a reserved judicious manner (on the other). The main problem is that the portion wasn't even close to meal sized. I felt like I was being punished for some unknown transgression. No table service for you Urqhart!!! And I hope you like your waffles extra small boy!!!!! MUAHHAAA!!! We ate silently as stroller after stroller bumped into our table. I must admit, I didn't at all agree with the rave reviews I read here; quite the contrary. Beau Monde is to Chhaya as Miles Davis is to Kenny G. As an aside, we've noticed most of the restaurants in the Passyunk square follow a bit of a motif. State Side, Plenty, Chhaya, Cantina, Birra...all entirely too hip for your own good. Owners need to do two things: 1. Go to a good pub in Europe (that's the hard one), and 2. go around the corner to Carmen's Country Kitchen. It's elevated, with a good deal less 'la-de-da', and one leaves feeling with the satisfaction of just having eaten a holiday meal. I don't care that all the restaurants in the square have artisan light bulbs. I don't care that the portions are stylishly lilliputian . I don't care that the napkins are made from recycled grocery bags. I truly, truly, with all my heart, don't care. I just want quality food (and enough to fill me up), sometimes a decent pint, at a good price. I'm putting the Passyunk Square on my no fly zone for the foreseeable future. Off to greener pastures.
label: NEG

text: This place started out great, but has gone downhill over the past few months. The quality of the cooking has significantly declined, which may be due to a change in the kitchen staff. Where the lunch combo portions used to be large and well-prepared, you will now usually get a few little pieces of beef or chicken, a gigantic pile of green onion stalks, and fat strips of onion stacked like cordwood. It is borderline nonsensical. Who eats finger-sized hunks of green onion? You are correct: No one. Well, no one of the genus and species to which West End Wok directly caters. This change has coincided with the Kafkaesque ability of West End Wok to deliver the wrong food to your table. In the course of one lunch, the host sat before me no less then four different people's lunches. Eventually, the roulette wheel clicked, and the appropriate plate of food was delivered. This odd characteristics contributes somewhat to the wonderful family atmosphere of the restaurant, but otherwise makes for inefficient mid-day substenance forays. And over time, the amount of rice granted with the combo has every so slowly decreased (as if the West End Wok is caught in the ancient parable about the length of eternity: Imagine a bird moving a Everest-sized mountain of sand one grain at a time). When this place first started, lunchtime loomed on my schedule like a bright, savory horizon - backlit with the sensous orange hue of sesame chicken. Now all is back to normal, and every now and then we visit the "somewhat decent Chinese place around the corner," hearts heavy with the memory of what this restaurant once represented - the dream, the tantalizing dream, of good Chinese food in the CWE. Note: Periodically the egg drop soup contains gray hunks of real, authentic fetal chicken. This is, of course, a delicacy in the Philippines. But I swore I would never eat fetal fowl again unless stuck on a jeepney in Quezon City. Proceed with caution. (I practice the squeeze test. Squeeze mysterious chunks with chopsticks. Overly firm chunks are most probably baby chicken.) Additional Note: The people at the register at West End Wok are very kind and welcoming people.

text: First let me start by saying, I've had some really good meals at Franco, and I was very much looking forward to going back. The scallops were not bad, but certainly lack any kind of flair or imagination. If you are going to do such a common started, make it unique, do something which makes it yours! I thought the salad was poorly flavored, but my wife liked it, so maybe it wasn't awful. For dinner we had the trout with couscous and mussels with fries. The muscles were so completely lacking in flavor, it was like chewing air. They were not bad per se., and even the consistency wasn't bad, but the taste was just completely lacking. Also, none of the fries were bigger than an inch long, so it felt like what we got was just the chunks that were left at the end of the night. The fish was a nice big serving and was probably the highlight of the meal. It wasn't the best thing I've ever had, but the amount of fish they provided and the fact that it wasn't offensive, made it pretty good in comparison. Sadly, the Couscous was so wet it was like chewing on a sponge. Probably need a lot more cooking time. The most shocking part of all this was that for as long as it took for our food to arrive (i.e. a LONG time, you would think that it would have been a lot better. Lastly, we had dessert...it was the low light of the meal. We had apple tart and something else which I've blocked out that used way too much almond paste; like it was going out of style. Anyway, they screwed up the apple tart...how do you screw up apple tart? It's virtually apple pie! If you can't do pie right, someone needs to find a new job! Huge chunks of apple in the tart (wrong size), poorly flavored (if at all), the crust was actually pretty well made, very light and flaky, but if the filler sucks, who cares. The whole experience was a freaking disappointment. I have no idea what happened at Franco, but change it back! It's really not a good things when the best you can say coming away from a meal was, "At least the bread was warm."

text: If I hadn't known via Yelp that this was where the old Butcher Boy's used to be, I would never have found it. Their signage is pretty difficult to spot, especially if you are driving on Virginia Street at 40 miles an hour. Inside, I was surprised to see how huge the restaurant was. And it's a sit down restaurant - I guess I was thinking I could quickly order a slice or two at the counter, then sit down and eat it and run out and do my errands. I felt weird just asking for a $2 slice of cheese pie and a $1.50 drink, and having to leave a tip on top of small amount. The staff there were very nice, though, so I gave them a hefty tip. The pizza was pretty good, and their pasta prices looked decent, so I'd like to come back for a real meal with friends. The restaurant is clean, if not cavernous, and they have cute little iron stands that are next to tables where you can hang your purse. It still floors me that a simple cheese pizza costs $12 in my hometown in NJ, and here you can't seem to find a decent one for less than $18. WHY, RENO, WHY?!!! I'll be curious to see if they will do well with the new Nu Yalk pizza opening up down the street in a few months.

text: So, I just tried this place as part of devour downtown, which is a great way to experience and test out some of indy's more "expensive" restaurants at a reasonable price. First off, our service was excellent. No complaints there. The building is great and I hear the roof top is wonderful. The restaurant was quiet, but not too quiet. Wine=excellent. The food is another story. The devour downtown menu offered several courses. For the appetizer I got a goat cheese and marinara sauce. The marinara sauce tasted like Ragu out of a jar. This was disappointing for me, given that I had ordered the mannicotti as my main dish (which also came with marinara). Barcelona Tapas offers this same dish and it's like a little slice of heaven. I also had a Caesar salad, which was probably one of the worst I have ever had. It was completely bland and the lettuce was actually warm. The mannicotti again tasted like it had Ragu on it. I had the chocolate Gelato for dessert and it was fantastic--almost tasted like dark chocolate, yum! It was the best part of the meal. My friend had the salmon over some sort of pasta as his main course. I tried the salmon (and I LOVE salmon), but it didn't taste fresh to me. It was also quite dry. I won't be going back. However, maybe their main menu is better? Personally, I didn't even think what I had was worth the $30. I had really high expectations for Dunaways, so I was quite disappointed when I tasted the food.

text: Finding a gym you like while balancing the cost of a membership is a never ending quest. I defected from LA Fitness out in Brandon and wanted to find a gym that was still "on the way" to home or work. First of all this is located on the bottom floor of some of the Channelside disctrict's condos. It's not a huge gym, but the layout works and there's a good selection of free weights, weight machines and cardio. The facility has steam rooms in the locker rooms, nice walk in showers with actual doors and plenty of lockers. They also have some hydro-massage stuff and tanning machines that I have never used. The place is cared for pretty damn well. The biggest gripe I had about LA Fitness is the stupid treadmills would get so beat up there was major slippage/torque problems with the belts and I'd stumble. This is not a problem here, I regularly see maintenance keeping the machines in top form. 4-5 of the treadmills have LCD tvs, but there are flat screens mounted to watch from the other machines. They have some TRX suspension training as well as some Spin type setup I have yet to try out as well. Both look interesting but I know the TRX is an additional charge. Pool access is available (located on the roof). Price, well... gyms are almost like going to buy a car. You definitely will need to bring your bargaining skills and pre-payment is king. Once you get past the haggling I think you will enjoy this place. Great facility, I normally shy away from the typical staff that work in gyms, but they are always friendly to me and greet me on my way in and out. Hours might not be up to snuff for some people, closing at 9pm on weekends and 11pm on weekdays (holidays are even more limited) may turn some elsewhere. Cannot beat this location if you live anywhere near Channelside, and don't worry about parking, you get 2 hours free in the actual condos garage. I ditch my car there even when I do runs around the neighborhood as well.
label: POS

text: Okay, first off the location here is awesome. Located in Sam Hughes Plaza practically across from the stadium it's walking distance to or from games. They always have the games on inside in case you want to skip the crowd. Now to the salad...All of them are great but my favorite by far is the Mediterranean. I have tried multiple times to duplicate this salad! All the ingredients are super fresh, and the feta is amazing. I don't know if they make their own dressing but this one is the bomb! I always ask for extra so I can stash some for home! Pizza. My goodness. The best I have EVER had. I've had lots and lots of pizza. Some from Chicago, California, all over and nothing compares to this! I always order the pepperoni, the use the cute little pepperonis like I used to eat as a kid. I swear they taste better than any other!! My husband LOVES the meatballs so we normally do half and half. The meatballs are huge, worth the additional price if you like meatballs. They use fresh mozzarella on the pizza, which IMO is what makes it so good. The pizza is super thin so in my mind it's healthier, thus I eat more. I recommend trying their white pizza too. From what the waitress told me it's olive oil and garlic with whatever topping you chose no sauce. I ordered a small just to give a try and now I have a hard time deciding on which pizza to chose every time I go! Lunch time is the best time to come here because they have great lunch specials. Well except for the fact that I can't substitute the salad they give you for lunch with the Mediterranean. I've asked and it's a hard no. Really chaps me too. Overall, amazing pizza, decent service, busy on game nights but worth the wait. Just be careful adding your toppings, they aren't cheap and add up quickly. I usually can't leave here for dinner without spending almost 50 bucks.

text: I've been hearing about this place and was excited to check it out with the beau. Sure the iPad ordering system is trendy, but sadly that's the only word I can use to describe our experience this time. First impressions upon walking in was good. Dim lighting, modern space, professionals chatting, social scene, girl's night kinda place, trendy. It was a Thursday night and we were seated right away. We perused the cool iPad menu and I have to applaud them for the ease of use. Simply select your item(s) and send the order to the kitchen at a tap of a button. Items are tapas style, so you can order the next item(s) at your own pace. Food came out incredibly fast. We also ordered a pitcher of sangria to share. Sangria: Served in a trendy french press and poured into wine glasses. Taste was sweet and tasted like a juice. Barely tasted any wine. Trendy appearance, but missing authenticity. Smoked Bacon & Artichoke Flatbread: Surprisingly, it was on the cold side. While it smelled good and served very quickly, it didn't taste fresh. Sorta like pizza under a heat-lamp. A little too pricey to be serving food quality like this, no? Four Cheese Satchels: Loved that they used arugula! This plate was most flavorful and was our favorite. The crispy pancetta was perfect on top of plentiful arugula and cheesy pockets. Spinach Gnocchi Marseilles: This smelled absolutely amazing when it came to the table. The sauce really made this stand out, but unfortunately, this was also the worst of the three dishes we ordered. I had two mussels in the dish (I think there were only a total of 3) and one was sandy and the other tasted rotten (had to spit both out). I'm not sure if mussels are in season, but I'm sorta embarrassed that this happened especially since I liked the sauce so much. The shrimp and scallops were good though. Four items later, our bill with 20% tip came out to be almost $60. So, basically it's a trendy restaurant/lounge without emphasis on the quality of food. Which says a lot because, after all, it's a restaurant and food comes first.
label: NEG

There may have been a more sizable crowd upstairs but I did not check it out. The space downstairs was laid back and looked just like a beer tavern should: low lighting, dark wood, long bar, tall bar stools. Chris behind the bar was very kind and patient with my perusing of the beer menu. He was able to come around periodically and offer suggestions. Ten minutes later when I decided what type of beer I wanted to try (no judging - the choices are endless) Chris gave me a couple of suggestions, one sample and led me happily to my perfect choice. I enjoyed the rest of my evening comfortably chillin and sipping on my well chosen beer. To cap off a great experience Chris even gave a mini science lesson when I asked what I felt rolling in a can of beer. Turns out it was a floating widget - used to release liquid nitrogen and provide better head quality!! So now I know --- I sound kinda beer snobbish right?? I will definitely be heading back - several times over.

text: This places are many good/great reviews, so please take my review however you'd like. And before I make it sound like I'm bashing our waiter, I will admit that I think he had a VERY demanding table that were running him ragged as they finished up their meals, and by the end of the night, he was extremely nice and chatted with us while we waited for our cab. We arrived at Flyte for an 8pm reservation. We were seated promptly by the hostess. We looked over our menus, trying to get an idea of what we wanted. We had already looked at the menus online and knew we wanted to start out with some cocktails before hand, but we were not given the cocktail menu when we were seated. No problem, we'll ask the waiter when he comes by. The problem was that the waiter didn't come by for over 10 min (again, there was a table next to us that was finishing up, and looked to be running him all over the place). When he finally did stop by and ask for the drinks, I asked him for a cocktail menu. He ran off to get one, and returned with it fairly quickly. Unfortunately, it wasn't the cocktail menu, it was a beer/spirits list. I then just pulled up the cocktail menu on my phone and passed it around. When he finally came back (we are now at about 25 min from when we were seated) we ordered our drinks and off he went. After several minutes (close to another 10) he came back and said, "your drinks are going to take awhile, I just wanted to let you know." It was at that point we decided to order our appetizers. Oh, he also asked at one point if we had been here before, we responded that we had not, and he proceed to go through every item on the menu, explaining every dish (more or less reading the menu with a few "everyone seems to love this" thrown in), really unnecessary. The cocktails (the Paris Manhattan and the Whiskey Smash were both excellent) and the appetizers came about 10 minutes after ordering. We started with the Slow poached eggs and bacon and the pork cheeks. Both of the appetizers were excellent. So things started looking up. We then ordered our entrees. My wife ordered the soup flyte and the butternut ravioli. She loved the ravioli, but thought the soups were rather bland. I ordered the Beef brisket. I thought it was good, but nothing special. The other couple with us ordered the sturgeon (which she raved about) and the duck breast with foie gras (he said the duck breast was good, but the foie gras was to much for the dish and they didn't pair well together, he just ate the duck breast separately). By the end of dinner, the place was empty. We asked the waiter if he could have the host call us a cab, which they were more than happy to do, and the waiter chatted with us while we waited for it. We never felt rushed, even though the night was over. Again, I don't want to blame the waiter for the excessive wait in the beginning, but everything together made this less than desirable.

text: Just read the comment from the owner on my review which I posted at the bottom of this update. Ilker, I read your menu very carefully even took a picture of it because of how insane it is. text: I've never written a negative review but here it is. Unfortunately, our visit was disappointing from start to finish. The hostess took forever to acknowledge us, then disappeared into the back for a long time. We had a reservation but she seated the walk-ins ahead of us. Then we sat as various wait staff passed us by before someone finally stopped, introduced themselves as our server and brought us water. The appetizers Las Favoritas (figs stuffed with chorizo and wrapped in bacon) and fried manchego cheese were quite yummy. However, that was pretty much all. My caipirinha had a thick layer of undissolved sugar at the bottom. My friend got the mussels ($15) which were rather fishy and soft. The garlic broth was the best part of it and there was not enough bread given to soak it up. We brought the broth home to put over rice. I got the special - quail in mole ($20), which sounded awesome but proved to be very disappointing. The one quail was really extra tiny, about as much meat as one drumstick, if that. The mole was okay, predominantly tomatoey, rather than the subtle flavors I associate with mole. The accompaniments were grilled green onions and some quinoa. They were both tasty, but seemed incredibly cheap and boring to serve as a special. I don't need monstrous portions but I was starving. the appetizers seemed priced appropriately for what you got but certainly not the disappointing dinners. If I go again (only if forced) I will do it tapas style with several small dishes instead. Sorry, Contigo. I really wanted to love you, but you've given me no reasons to whatsoever.

text: After having logged enough hours at Tapestry, I feel confident enough to say that it is a wonderful bar/restaurant in my neighborhood and I'm hoping it will stay around for a while. The cocktails are superb, the beer selection is stellar and the food does not disappoint. It's a great spot to meet up with friends or even to have a fun dinner with that special someone. I really thought it was going to be hard to top the previous offering (Adsum) but Tapestry has found a way to breathe new life into this space. The decor is similar because they kept a lot of the existing layout. The colors are deep and rich blacks and the whole spot just feels a bit more inviting than it ever did before. For the small plates, I really like the bacon wrapped dates and the sweet potato fries are actually crispy. I've had a number of other items on the menu as well and I've also stopped people at the bar to ask what they are eating. The staff here understands presentation and flavor and it makes for a great experience. I'm a fan, I'm a regular and will continue to be, for as long as possible.

text: Offended on so many levels at the poor display of service and, for lack of a better word, DISCRIMINATION. I'll summarize as quickly as I can. One of our girls decided to dance on the stage, and as soon as she got on stage we hear a "booo" from this male patron. And while that guys comment is in no way connected to the service of this establishment, at that moment the tone of discomfort and feeling unwelcome was set. So the girl decided to pull one of the guys on stage with her to dance. A worker promptly advised my friend that he wasn't permitted to be on the stage....not a big deal, as we know that's customary at most bars/clubs. In the mean time, several other guy patrons (of a lighter complexion) were also on the stage with their respective dance partners, so my friend decided to get back on stage and dance with the aforementioned girl friend. As a result, he was once again ask to leave the stage, followed by a "lecture" on the side of the stage (an additional service that none of the other lighter complexioned patrons were receiving). By this time, we had had enough and one of my friends decided to express his disdain for how the situation was being handled. As a result of him raising and expressing his concerns, we were escorted out of the bar. Once outside, we asked to speak to the manager and were given misleading information by a guy who claimed to be the manager, only after he lied about his name (gave 2 different names when we were inquiring as to his name and position) and basically ignored and avoided addressing our request. As a young professional, I've never been so disgusted and humiliated by an establishment. I understand that establishments reserve the right to refuse admission and service in situations where guests are unruly. However, I don't feel that expressing your concerns and opinions to the staff is an unruly gesture. Neither do I think that it is grounds for the humiliation we experienced at The Red Rooster in Nashville. I will never put myself through that again, nor will I invest another dollar of my money in this discriminatory establishment.

text: Alright, now this New Yorker can say that I've tried Shake Shack. I know, what the heck? I've never eaten at the infamous Shack Shake (now with many NYC locations)?! Yeah, well, I don't like waiting on line for food. I've also only recently started eating burgers (cue gigantic *gasp* and fainting in shock). So the Philly location spurred our friends to invite us to try them, and I thought why not? I decided to make sure we wouldn't be waiting on a line for freaking ever by getting there kinda early for dinner on a Thursday, and there was barely a line leading out of the door. I actually let people go ahead of me while waiting for the others to show. Of course no space inside to eat, so Rittenhouse Park provided us with a venue to eat. I was surprised by the size of the burgers - tiny! - but at least my bird dog was a regular size. Split and grilled, it had a nice snap with each bite. Everyone else obviously got one of their burgers (Shackburgers and Smokeshack) with fries, and our friends got chocolate and strawberry shakes. They were drooling over the burgers from the first bite, and at the end of the meal declared they could definitely eat another, despite being full. Fries were fine (they really liked them), and our friends loved the shakes and how thick they were. A nice burger addition to the area - but thank god the park is so close! Every bench had people eating Shake Shack as we walked through :)

Okay, so I'm eating a huge burger with fried sides and soda... at least I can make one little healthy choice. :) Everything came out exactly as ordered. Even when the restaurant was busy on a Saturday at lunchtime, our food came out faster than we expected. The french fries are on the thin side, and were cooked nicely both times we ordered them. Dad's choice, the haystack onions, were much better than I expected. They were very thin, delicately breaded onion "rings". Hot & tasty. Based on their success with sides, I plan to try the veggie frites (with fried asparagus, green beans, and carrot sticks) and the sweet potato fries on future visits. The root beer float, as you can see in one of the photos I took, was served with scooped vanilla ice cream in a frosty glass accompanied by a bottle of root beer. Very nice! As a big soda drinker, I appreciate the soda fountain available for customers to refill drinks. I also liked the 'to go' cup so I could take some soda on the road. One thing that brings Smashburger up a notch from Five Guys and other "burger" spots is that the staff is so attentive. Service was pretty good. The server arrived promptly as we sat and lit the centerpiece lantern. If you looked really hard, you could detect little rays of light coming out of the tiny holes on its sides. Our table was just as dark as it was before. At the server's suggestion, I picked the Mole Poblano. The menu described the sauce as "truly rich and complex" with flavor, complementing "[a] succulent boiled chicken breast exalted from the past." However, when my dish came out, the chicken was dry and flavorless. All of its juices and flavors "from the past" had been drained out. The sauce was also unbelievably dry and flavorless. The food description was not even close! My boyfriend's Cochinita Pibil was also dry and overcooked. His ceviche special was delicious, though. And his parents' fish dish was also tasty. We didn't stay for dessert. Lesson 2: avoid the mole poblano. On the plus side, our drinks were brought to our table, on a tray balanced on the server's head. text: I am disposed to love a spa. Spas, to me, are for the experience: woo-woo music in the background, clean, crisp surroundings, towels I can't afford, manufactured serenity--I love it all. This is why I was completely shocked by my experience here. I expected to be swaddled in a nubbly bathrobe and marched directly to luxurious pummeling, followed by an easy dip in a hot tub and generally amoeba-ing around in relaxation. I was excited as I stood in the lobby, waiting for my staff member to conduct me to the locker room. There were perfumes and fancy pillows all over the place, and it was about what I expected from something like this. The rest of it, however, was rather unimpressive. The trek to the locker room bluntly leads into the gym, and the locker room itself is about what I'd expect from the average YMCA/JCC/gym. The bathrobes are terry cloth, which isn't so bad, but these were thin and rough. Not quite the nubbly awesomeness I was expecting. Then, my friend and I kind of wandered awkwardly into the lobby (with grand front doors that face the street) but stood there in our robes while we tried to figure out if it was "okay" to enter what we thought was the "spa portal." Mind you, we were shivering, naked but for our robes, and just... awkward. Most spas have a tastefully hidden pathway from locker rooms to spa area. The Guerlain Spa of New Orleans, however, does not. Abrupt transitions abound. The "spa portal" was actually the best part of the experience, which in this case was a room filled with Guerlain products, giant comfy chairs, and trashy magazines galore. This room I liked. I was quickly retrieved from this room and led to another--actually gorgeous--concourse filled with the therapy rooms, and was introduced to the most awful massage therapist I have ever encountered. The massage. Oh, the massage. It was awful. The appointment did not begin with a discussion of problem areas, there were no questions about possible injuries, no consultation of any kind. Instead, I was hurried under the blanket, and then manhandled for an hour. I have never ended a massage without thinking, "Damn, I hate that this is over." That is, until now, when I winced my way through what can only be described as an utterly painful experience. I asked her repeatedly to reduce the pressure of the massage, but she did not reach a level that was tolerable. I almost thought she was angry at me. Is that neurotic? I kept thinking maybe it was me, maybe I was missing the point of the "style," but a massage therapist friend told me afterward that my experience was completely inappropriate. When the massage was over, my MT ushered me quickly down the hall and through the "buy our stuff!" area (completely bypassing the fancy coffee distribution kiosk!), leading me by arm straight to the locker room. She walked off without a word. I understand that, you know, having a problem with your *spa experience* is a pretty snotty first-world problem to have. Here's the thing: I like massages. I work a lot. I wanted to treat myself to a luxurious experience to celebrate the new year. I said, "Yeah, this massage is expensive as shit, but it will HAVE to be amazing." I've been to spas before, and they are always comfortable, welcoming, new age-y, and generally overwhelmingly pleasant. This is the most expensive massage I've ever purchased, and the experience wasn't even lackluster--it was downright bad. Being rushed through the premises, barely acknowledged by the massage therapist, pummeled within an inch of my muscles' lives, given cheaply-made robes and towels, through a structure that is awkwardly constructed and dumps customers into abrupt transitions from public spaces to private, all of these things created the most awful spa experience I've ever had. I'm not sure why I'm giving it two stars. Maybe they get an extra star for not being infested with roaches or something. And the final blow? There isn't even a readily accessible hot tub or sauna from the locker room. I hate sounding rednecky, but these creature comforts tend to come with the giant price tag.

text: Alright, there's a new guy in town when it comes to Southeastern Asian groceries. There are many things different about the Bangkok Market, compared to various Asian markets around Nashville (not to mention the USA). It's extremely clean, and I'd even go as far as to say beautifully designed. Word on the street is there was an interior designer involved in the creation of the Bangkok Market... I immediately noticed upon entering that something was missing from this Asian market, something prevalent in maybe any other Asian market you'll encounter. You know, the smell.. The smell of raw chicken and fish - not to be found at Bangkok. Why? Well owner, Pornchai, in our conversation stressed how important it is for the place not to smell, and so he doesn't plan on selling those items. Though there is an extremely diverse selection of frozen animal products in the produce section, including Asian whole fish and black chicken. Yes, BLACK chicken!! Did you know this even existed?? I was told it has a cleaner taste than the common yellow, and is most often used for medicinal purposes. I touched on my "conversation" with the owner. Well, it was more like a personalized tour of the entire store. Why I was so lucky to get this opportunity I have no idea, but Pornchai walked me through the whole store and described many of the items to me and went into detail about Thai cooking I'd never considered. I didn't know there are coconut milks with different fat percentages (and I'm not talking about what is known as "light coconut milk" - Pornchai laughed at my mention of "light' coconut milk!), the ones with lower percentages to be used for soups, and the ones with higher percentages to be used for thicker stronger curries and soups. And some even designated for desserts... In our conversation Pornchai stressed that many of the foods offered in the store are chemical and preservative-free, which seems to be an important point at the Market. I don't think I've ever seen coconut milk in small cans - cans which have just enough for a recipe, so you're not stuck with leftover coconut milk and no idea what to do with it. Bangkok Market has these. Also, I have never seen teeny cans of zillions of different curry pastes - only jars of red and green - but Bangkok Market has got ALL flavors ... and I was gifted with one of each to sample. Red, green, yellow, massaman, and panang. Holy HELL. It's gonna be a curry-eatin' year for me, which apparently has more health benefits than I knew - I was told that Thai and Indian people have a very low risk of Alzheimer's disease, and the proof seems to be in the curry (as opposed to the pudding). The first time I even noticed Bangkok Market existed was when I was driving to Home Depot, and just before making the right turn onto Powell Dr., I did a double take when I saw the Bangkok Market sign and said, "What the...?!" It's new and it's awesome; I just hope it lasts despite it's unassuming location.

text: I recently purchased a blighted property with my siblings in Mid-City. We are historically renovating the property. We began plumbing the building and planned on replacing the existing water meter, which has not been updated since the house was originally built in 1910, with two new meters and new pipes that funnel to our water meters. I spoke to the House Connections department in SWBNO and she quoted the installation cost between $1,800 and $2,500. She explained that sometimes an installation can cost upwards of $5,000 for a meter installation, but we would only have to pay $2,500 at the most. I received the estimate ten days later: $5,068.20. This was only for one meter and we would have to pay the whole amount. When I tried to understand why it was so drastically different from the other prices I was given, they explained that it is never the SWBNO's policy to give clients average price estimates, even though two of her employees already had, and she referred me to master of maintenance. The master of maintenance had very little insight as to how the water meter installation prices were actually determined. He said this was the SWBNO's primary contractor's domain: Fleming Construction. He said Fleming Construction set the prices and SWBNO followed suit. He tried to help to the best of his ability, but the reality was that he merely managed SWBNO's contract with Fleming. I called Jefferson Parish's water board to see how much they charged for installing a one-inch water meter. They charge a flat rate of $1,500. The city pays for the pipes on public property and the homeowner pays for the portion within their property line. I discovered that most municipalities across America operate in the same fashion (Chicago, Illinois, Tucson, Arizona), and some counties go as far as incur all of the costs for new meter installation, because they regard it as standard updating and maintenance of infrastructure. Other city's water utilities provide thorough pricing schedules for different types of water meter installation scenarios. The pricing reasoning is well documented and fully accessible to the customer. This creates a predictable and fair planning environment. SWBNO's policy of expecting homeowners to foot the entire bill for maintenance and updates that should have already occurred stands in direct opposition to Mayor Landrieu and the City Council's goal of fighting blight, fixing the condition of our deteriorating streets, and minimizing city operating costs. Investors require a predictable and transparent city government. Most investors can absorb a certain amount of variable costs, but I doubt that after someone has purchased a home, and then secured a construction loan like we have, that they will be liquid enough to pay a little over $10,000 to partially subsidize a municipal service that should have been maintained. As a historic district, most of the Mid-City housing stock boasts water meters from when the neighborhood was initially drained in the 1910's. We later discovered that our existing meter was made of toxic lead. If we ever hope to address the chronic blight that has pre-dated 2005, then we must not penalize would-be investors by forcing them to pay for the mistakes of a mismanaged bureaucracy. We must fairly and efficiently address our infrastructure while also mending the structural issues of the SWBNO that have culminated in this citywide crisis. I am not an engineer, economist, or a city planner, but since no one in the SWBNO seems to hold these credentials either, I feel equally qualified in stating that updating the pipes in such a piece-meal fashion will ultimately waste time and money for the city and Orleans Parish taxpayers. In my subsequent dealings with the SWBNO I learned that it contracts out all of their engineering, maintenance, and pavement repairs to private contractors. The employees manning their offices have no immediate access to these contracts, making it impossible for home and business owners to coordinate reasonable time schedules for repairs and updates occurring on or near their properties. As the city considers another price increase for the SWBNO's services I believe we must seriously consider what services they actually provide. Much scrutiny has been directed towards the SWBNO's Director Marcia St. Martin's salary, pension plan, and performance as a director. They are well-deserved critiques and must not be abandoned. Further inspection should also be directed toward the employees of the SWBNO. There are undoubtedly many hardworking and experienced individuals at the SWBNO, but I believe those who are none of those things outnumber them by a great majority. The Sewerage and Water Board of New Orleans is not just another utility company. It is charged with working against extraordinary subsidence, functioning as a stopgap against disease spurred on by standing water, and keeping our city from drowning when it rains. We have to expect better.

text: Possibly the worst real estate company out there. This is how the company works: You call and are assigned an office agent. The office agent is great, the so-called 'bait' for which you fall for. He is interested, knowledgeable, will match you with apartments that fit your needs. Then you go to see an apartment, and only one real estate agent out in the field is assigned to show that particular apartment so you have to work with them to schedule a viewing. If you like the apartment, you then pay an application fee (the most expensive in town, $50 per person) and are assured they will get back to you in 48 hours. WARNING: by applying, you also have to provide a one month deposit in the form of a certified check, and if you are approved and do not move in, for whatever reason, they reserve the right to keep your one month deposit. Once you are approved you will work once again with the listing agent (the one who showed you the place) to get your contract signed and voila, the apartment is yours. In essence, it sounds simple enough, but is, however, completely dependent on who your listing agent is. In our case, the company took 1 week to let us know if we were approved (from later conversations with the owner of the place, he wasn't even aware we existed until the lease was made), and then took 3 more weeks to produce a lease, that then took another week to alter with the things we had specifically requested when we applied for the apartment, which ultimately cost us a 'free month if lease signed by x' as we clearly signed three weeks after that due date. In the meantime, two other units had rented through another real estate company and the owner was just as flabbergasted as we were. Thank you, phillyaptco, for making what could have been a streamlined process, into an extremely harrowing, stressful, and painful process. I understand that it all depends on who your listing agent is, but that is exactly why this model doesn't work. You need to have one person in charge of everything for you, of selecting places, then showing them to you, then running your credit and then producing a lease, to have any sort of reasonable expectation that they will be held accountable for you. Veer away. In most cases the owners of a place will be working with more than one real estate company. Look up the address on the internet and go with more respectable companies that will be oh-so-much less painful.
label: NEG

text: Went there for lunch and was very disappointed with the pizza--Ive had better pizza in a homeless bar in Yuma. Not what I would expect for an upscale Italian Restaurant. Thought, heck, I'll give them a second chance..so my wife and I went for the supper service. We ordered the Bruschetta appetizer, it was just ok, nothing great. Our Caesar salads had no taste whatsoever, to the point neither of us even attempted to finish it. I ordered the Chicken Milano, which was good , but it had an inordinate amount of cheese sauce. My wife ordered the Seafood Stuffed Orange Roughy with a cheese sauce ($23) and when it came out we thought it was a mistake. Usually when a fillet it stuffed, it is split and filled, in this case it should have been filled with shrimp, scallops and crab meat. The waitress came with the manager and asked if everything was ok, I was asked if the order was wrong? We could not find any shrimp or scallops, it was a flat fillet with a breading layer and cheese over it all. The manager pointed out it was "minced" seafood, not whole shrimp etc...well, after a search we found a few shreds of crab meat and that was it. My wife had eaten half of it looking for the seafood, she didn't want another dish, so she declined that (nice of the restaurant), but there was no offer to take a portion of the check off or comp a dessert..btw she didn't finish the fish either after the great minced seafood search. The service was ok, the prices are not in line for the food and there is a lack of flavor in everything they serve. Not worth dropping $60 on and leaving with a bad taste in our mouth. text: Avoid this place!! Also, this is NOT my first time in NOLA. I went here to get some BBQ shrimp (their signature dish, according to the rather dull menu). She said, and note the quotes, "they are served in a red, soupy sauce". Swear!!! I'm like "HuuuuHHH?" Needless to say they came out and the sauce was OK, but the shrimp?? First off there was everything from popcorn size to prawns. OK fellow cooks, what are the chances they all cooked perfectly? Yeah, the big ones where cooked OK, the small ones.... you guessed it...overcooked. Now let's talk about quality. They were impossible to peel. For those of you who have never have traditional NOLA BBQ shrimp they are cooked whole, meaning, with the heads on. But just like crawfish, they are great this way and SHOULD be easy to peel and eat. Not these. I fought with them until i had enough. I'm assuming they were NOT fresh, thus the reason the meat had fused to the shell. I also ordered red beans and rice. No seasoning and little taste. The sauce the beans where in, was so watery. Look some advice for the cooks (i assume there hasn't been a chef in the kitchen in a while), drain the bean water out of the can, when you open your canned beans. The bread seemed fresh....the butter prepackaged. SCORE! 1.5 stars. Won't be back...I'll be at Pascal's Manale!!

text: Let me first say what this bar with a burger joint in it is not. It is not a coddled white tablecloth environment, with a bathroom attendant. IT IS A DIVE BAR. Which to me is perfect. I must say it seems like the grill is a bit detached from the bar. Yes they are connected, but the grill has a life of it's own. Think hard working guys cranking out amazing burgers. I had the Peanut butter burger. Why? Because where else can you have that? Life is too short to eat at Appleby's. Experience new things. They have a great selection of Tequila. text: I am like...89% sure everyone who waits tables here is stoned most of the time. And really, that's okay. The service can get weird sometimes, but I never feel too weird being here. I recognize all the trappings of crust punks and bike punks, despite the gutter punk decor. (Hot tip: gutter punks don't like having jobs. It gets in the way of harassing tourists on Frenchmen St.) Then again, this is probably not the place to bring your sweet church-going mother unless she's okay with a server who has been around the block a few times...on a fixie. (Hot tip: hipsters aren't the only ones with fixies.) I should probably talk about the food and not just the servers, amirite? Okay. There is a lot of food. I know this sounds simple and stupid, but bear with me. The food comes in large quantities. Larger than average. Larger than New Orleans typically spews forth. So get your tum ready or take a box home. (I double-fisted a burrito one night, and I still brought some home for later.) And there are vegetarian options. Like, real ones. Granted, they read like a stoner dreamt them up in a haze of really good purple kush (that's a type of pot, right?); but darn if they aren't tasty. I recommend the Mardi Gras Indians if you're feeling tacos. Here is your super-pro tip about hot sauce: There are multiple bottles of spicy liquid available for your consumption. If you think you have what it takes to go toe-to-toe with the big boys (and girls) of hot sauce, ask your server for the really spicy one. They'll usually say, "Oh, I brought you the hot sauce." That's when you look at them calmly and request, again, the REALLY spicy one. This will usually get you what you want. Also, for the confused: this is a Creole Taquería. That means it's not any real sort of food; this place is a mash-up. A good one. If I were about to make a musical comparison, I might compare Juan's to the Grey Album by DJ Danger Mouse: smooth, splendid, not to everyone's taste. Sometimes, you just need the classics. (Oh god, this review reads like I'm stoned.) Accessibility notes: Half of the restaurant is accessible for mobility devices. The men's restroom is not accessible because it is up a step. Ditto for the bar. No braille signage or menus. Can get super loud at peak hours. Most of the booths are narrow and difficult to get into.
label: POS

It was a barely noticeable blemish on my back that ended up being basal cell carcinoma. Basal cells grow in and out so even if you have a small freckle-like mole it could be big underneath the skin. I had the MOHs surgery here and everything went great. Not all dermatologist offer MOHs since its newer technology. Glad that this place does. If you live in California and tan or have blonde hair you should have your moles checked out once a year. I'm in my early thirties & never thought I'd have skin cancer, but I'm grateful to have a good dermatologist who knows what they are doing. text: Back when ML was on Delmar, I would have considered 5 stars, but I still think it lost a smidgen of personality in the move. That being said, I still love the food, prices, and service! Since they offer some more familiar Chinese dishes, it's good for a group that might include some non-adventurous folks. I also love to occasionally order the Hot & Sour soup from that menu. It's delicious and a smaller portion than many of their Vietnamese soups, which are wonderful but better to either share or get as an entree. My absolute favorite dish is the Bo Luc Lac with its high quality, perfectly cooked seared beef. Also good are the spring rolls, the roasted duck with a ginger garlic sauce (vit quay), and the curry duck soup (vit ca ry). The prices are reasonable, and I always have leftovers for the next day. Some of my friends have commented on higher prices and smaller portions. Maybe it's somewhat true, but nothing more than most restaurants have had to implement with rising food costs and a tough economy. It's still very affordable with more than enough food. Service there is friendly and SO fast! Even on my last visit, with a full house, they checked up on us regularly and had our food out quickly. The menu is vast and has thorough descriptions and numbers that correspond to each dish. Even though I like to give the pronunciation of my dish a try, I always use the number as well just to be clear. The servers do speak English, but it can be slow going if you have questions or want more details. Be patient- they are very helpful and kind.

text: Slim Goodies is located on a "cool" stretch of Magazine St., close to American Apparel, Buffalo Exchange and Breaux Mart. The omelets are delicious, a fluffy egg pancake cradling a variety of yummy fresh fillings. One of my favorites is the Americana, stuffed with peppers, onions, bacon and cheddar cheese. The perfect combination. The hash browns are pretty good, but remember to order them well done if you want them to be crispy. I've never had the Jewish Coonass (latkes with crawfish), but one day I'll gather up enough courage to order it with a straight face. The coffee is good, the prices and low, and the service is exactly what you need at a place like this: friendly and fast. That makes Slim Goodies a winner in the category of no-fuss breakfast.
